## What changed from r3.5 (r3.6; RB12-CLOSE-5: the retirement rule, the canonical spelling of a hex key, the names and the reach of the dependents check, the deadline of the hop-tick loop) [r3.6:L]

Tags `[r3.6:H<n>]`. H13 (manifest item 7): the retirement of an earlier `policy.owner` / `policy.setRootHistory` row is defined exactly - its last valid block is the smaller of its stored `validToBlock` and the appended row's `validFromBlock` - 1 - and a row that ends before it starts (`validToBlock` < `validFromBlock`) is refused. H14 (manifest item 7): a 32-byte hex key has one spelling (`0x` + 64 lower-case digits); the Go side refuses any other spelling of a `generations` key as `contract_identity_manifest_corrupt` instead of lower-casing it. H15 (manifest item 7): the abbreviations `manifest_unknown` / `manifest_shadow` of the tables are the codes `contract_identity_manifest_unknown{chain}` / `contract_identity_manifest_shadow{table,key}`, and the dependents check is judged on the merged manifest as a whole (Go authoritative; the CI tooling is a subset check). H16 (E1b): the tick loop's deadline for an anchor with several members is the LATEST pending `memberChainDeadline`; with no deadline known the reach bound stays the only stop. No table of Items 1, 3, 4 or 5 is touched: states, vocabulary and the vector index lift byte-identical, and no container byte, no manifest byte and no published vector set changes.

## What changed from r3.4 (r3.5; RB12-CLOSE-1: the settlement rule ids, the missing-code answer of step 18, the message_root annotation) [r3.5:L]

Tags `[r3.5:H<n>]`. H11: the new Freeze item 5 row `VS8-126` and the step 18 text say what step 18 answers when the container has no section in `codes` for `A`, `V` or `G` of an attest station (`U unproven{code_not_carried}` on `authorization_attest`; step 12 answers `R code_unproven_bytes` on `code_identity`; the headline is `refused`). H12: `message_root` is annotated as never printed as the `field` of an `R registry_mismatch` (F17 prints a pre-only change of `A14` as `U state_changed_in_block{A14}`).

## What changed from r3.3 (r3.4; RB12-R34, one batched revision: the seven contradictions S1-S7 and the four low defects D1-D4 of `checkins/V-RB12-COMPLETENESS.md`, S1 of `checkins/V-RB12-MANIFEST.md`, and the four findings of the capture-3c package) [r3.4:L]

Tags `[r3.4:H<n>]`. H1 (S1, D1): `message_root` is not an R field: it is the registry-link detector of a pre-only change of `A14`, printed as `U state_changed_in_block` by F17; the text now says so and the vector `VS8-151.message_root` exercises that branch (removing the value made that vector fail: the registry link was then `verified`). H2 (S2): the state row ids `attest_calldata_undecodable` and `authority_level_unproven` are rows of `states.json`, carried by no report field. H3 (S3, D3): step 13 evaluates the step-19(d) registry rules at N and the vocabulary `alert field` gains `registered`, `power`, `total_power`. H4 (S4, D2): every simultaneous violation at N is its own Open entry, in a fixed order. H5 (S5): step 19, an active owner with no violated rule. H6 (S6): `VS8-155` states that the key swap persists at N. H7 (manifest S1): the manifest writer gate covers the anchor and the verifier only; `CertenAccountV7_3` is outside it. H8 (3c findings a-d): the E1b reach, the one-proof double use of a tick, the reach stop of the tick loop and the reorged-tick policy. H9 (S7): the vector ids `VS8-090` and `VS8-100` used by the 2c set are not index rows; they are `VS8-220.n_only_hole` and `VS8-172.owner_active_in_block_prepost`. D4 (`code_not_carried`) is a vector-side classification, not a spec text change.

## What changed from r3.2 (r3.3; RB12-GOINTEGRATE, one batched revision found by running every published set through the composed verifier) [r3.3:L]

## Trust base and stated residuals (new in r2; A1, A6)

S8's claim is *"the contracts that attested and settled this leg are the published builds at pinned addresses, under the rules in force when they judged"*. Inputs trusted (as `PROOF_V2` s.1 / `00_STANDARD.md:35-39`): the target chain's own consensus (through S7 `finalized`), standard cryptography, and the **manifest** (an embedded, hash-pinned file from this repository - the same status as S7's pins). The contract owner is **not** a trust input: the owner's actions are *checked*, not assumed (rule IB closes the intra-block window; `policy.owner` pins who the owner is; the registry is emitted and linked). What remains, always printed in every report as `residuals` (fixed texts, not "open parts", because they are properties of the contract design, not of this evidence):

- **R-PKC**: `authorizedPubkeyCommitments[pkc]` is an owner-authorized set of aggregate-key commitments; the contract does not derive that the authorized commitments correspond to signer subsets of at least 2/3 power (`CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:2229-2233`; live: 29 = C(7,5)+C(7,6)+C(7,7) authorized, M3). S8 proves the used `pkc` was authorized at B_v with binding enforced; where S9 exposes the signers' recomputed commitment S8 requires it equals `pkc` (step 21d). It does not prove the owner authorized only quorum subsets. [r3:S2-1] The authorized set is proven **exactly** only on the `manifest_history` route (no `Registry9`): the row's `pkcList` has `pkcCount` distinct entries, every listed commitment is proven `true` at B_v-pre and B_v-post, and slot 5 equals `pkcCount`; since slot 5 changes with every flag change (`CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:1861-1873`, the only writer of slot 4 and 5), no further entry can be `true`. On every other route only the used `pkc` is proven authorized; the rest of the set cannot be enumerated from storage proofs (a mapping has no key list; reconstructing it from `PubkeyCommitmentAuthorized` events would need one receipt proof per historical call) and stays this residual, printed in every report.
- **R-INNER**: the Groth16 public inputs carry `signedVotingPower/totalVotingPower` from the proof blob, and no code compares them with the anchor's recomputed outer numbers (F-S8-8; `CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:2216-2217` vs `BLSZKVerifierV2_1.sol:250-253`). S8 reports equality; inequality is an `alert` (step 19f).
- **R-SETTLE-POINTER**: the account's anchor pointer is mutable by `setAnchorContract` (`onlySelf`); S8 reads it at N (post-state), not at the instant of TX3's `_authorizeLeaf` (`[REV]` matrix line 45). A pointer change by the account's own self-call inside the settlement block, **or by an earlier OR a later transaction of block N** [r3.1:D6], is not excluded by a block-boundary read (state root N is the END-of-block state). [r3:S2-5] The same residual covers the account's other mutable authorization words that step 14 reads at N: `_operationRequirements` (slot 8), `_pageLevel` (9), `_pageLevelSet` (10), all written only by `onlySelf` functions (`CertenAccountV7_3.sol:748-764`, AST writer table in M20). A leg whose target is the account itself is detected and named (`authority_level` `U self_call_leg`). [r3.1:D6] What the code does about the level words, and no more: the receipt of the settlement carries the level the contract USED (`GovernanceOperationExecuted` / `GovernanceBatchExecuted`, declared `CertenAccountV7_3.sol:258-270`, emitted at `:460`, `:497`, `:500`), and step 14 requires the level recomputed from the N-state words to EQUAL it; a difference is `U authority_level_unproven{level_differs_from_logged}`. So `_pageLevel` / `_pageLevelSet` cannot silently differ from the level used. What stays in the residual: (i) the anchor pointer (nothing logs it); (ii) `_operationRequirements` (the required levels are not logged, so a later transaction of block N that changed them is not detected by the equality; the successful receipt shows that the contract's own check passed at execution, and the `required` S8 prints is read at N).
- **R-WRITERS** [r3.1:D5]: the claim "no transaction of B_v changed an authorization word and reverted it" (rule IB) rests on the member-level writer extraction of the pinned builds (`builds[].authWriters`, produced from the solc AST by the manifest generator and re-checked by `verify-identity-manifest.sh`). [r3.4:H7] Scope of the writer gate: the generated writer sets (`authwriters.*`) exist for `CertenAnchorV8_2` and `BLSZKVerifierV2_1` only; `CertenAccountV7_3` is outside the manifest writer gate (it cannot pass the extractor: OpenZeppelin `StorageSlot` assembly is on the fail-closed list) and this spec claims no writer proof for the account's words. The extractor, the solc compiler and the AST it reads are trusted code: its negative controls (an honest contract that passes, 16 seeded defects that each fail exactly the stated condition, `design/vectors/s8/negctl/`, M32) show what it detects, not that it detects every Solidity construct; the extractor fails closed on the hazard classes listed in the mechanical premise (`delegatecall`, `callcode`, `selfdestruct`, assembly `sstore` / `create` / `create2` / `delegatecall` / `callcode` / `selfdestruct`, storage pointers and lvalue roots it cannot attribute, indirect calls, declared function types, a reassigned guard key) and on nothing else; a construct outside those classes that writes an AUTH member through a path the walker does not follow is not detected [r3.2:D14]. A build whose writers the extractor cannot attribute, or whose allow-list is wider than the verifier's frozen one, is never rule-IB-verified (`build_without_writer_proof`).

## Answers

### Q0. Verdict on the runbook design (confirm / refute against the source) - what the source requires instead

The runbook Phase C (RB12 s.C, items 1-4) proposes: evidence beside the settlement; account proofs + full runtime code + storage proofs for the F2 slot list at the **settlement block's** state root; compare with the manifest; report S8 at S7's level. Confirmed: the structure (evidence beside the settlement, code bytes hashed to the proven codeHash, masked hash vs the manifest, immutable rules, S7 level binding, S9 keys via the registry). **Refuted / corrected by the source (each is a finding, F-S8-n):**

| id | what the source requires instead | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| F-S8-1 | The BLS quorum is evaluated in a **different transaction (and block) from the settlement**: TX1 `createBatchAnchor` stores the record; TX2 `executeComprehensiveProof` runs `_verifyBLSProof`/`_verifyBLSQuorum` (registry, powers, threshold, `pubkeyBindingEnforced`, `authorizedPubkeyCommitments`, set root in the signed message) and only then sets `proofExecuted`; TX3 (the account settlement) reads only `anchors[id].valid && proofExecuted`, `verifyProof` and its own anchor pointer. State at the settlement block therefore cannot show the rules the quorum was judged under: the owner can change set, threshold, binding or commitments between TX2 and TX3. S8 needs a second station at the **attestation block** B_v. The settlement does not come at a fixed distance after the attestation: the gap is bounded only by the leaf's `notAfter` (`[C]:CertenAccountV7_3.sol:587`, bound into the leaf) and the relayer's `proof.expiresAt` (`:536`), both set by the system - a settler has a 30 min window and a takeover settles about 50 min after the attestation (`[V]:pkg/execution/batch_settlement_window.go:33,68`), which is more than one EIP-2935 window on Base post-Denim (27.3 min, M14); live gaps measured 1-7 blocks (Measurements M1). (r1 said "the contract bounds nothing": corrected in r2.) | `[C]:evm/src/core/CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:847-905` (createBatchAnchor), `:1316-1367` (executeComprehensiveProof), `:2102-2160` (`_verifyBLSProof`), `:2181-2232` (`_verifyBLSQuorum`); `[C]:evm/src/account/CertenAccountV7_3.sol:512-540` (`_verifyAnchorUsable`: `anchors(...)` destructure, `require(valid && proofExecuted)` at :531), `:572-592` (`_authorizeLeaf`) |
| F-S8-2 | The account **leaf does not bind the account address** (domain, chainid, `adiURLHash`, commitment, operationID, book, page, window). A copy of the account bytecode deployed anywhere with the same `adiURL` and a pointer to the real anchor can consume the same leaf and execute the same call from its own address. `_consumedLeaf` is per account (`CertenAccountV7_3.sol:237`, consumption `:586-591`), so S6's "consumed once" is "once per account address": an impostor account can re-spend a leaf the real account already consumed. S8 must therefore prove **account provenance** (the executing account is the factory-created account of that ADI), not only account code; that is what makes S6's replay statement mean "once". | `[C]:CertenAccountV7_3.sol:365-384` (`computeLeaf`), `:322-327` (`initializeAnchor` is permissionless once), `[C]:CertenAccountFactoryV11.sol:195,264-268` (factory binds the anchor at deployment; `_adiToAccount` registry), `:90-92` |
| F-S8-3 | RB12-B finding 10, second half is **refuted**: the anchor calls the *view* `blsZKVerifier.verifyBLSSignature(bytes,bytes32)` (never `verifyBLSSignatureProof`), which does not read the `verifiedProofs` cache (slot 5). The first half stands: the verifier enforces its **own** `storedThreshold*` (slots 0, 1) and `owner` (slot 2) on the path. S8 proves slots 0, 1, 2 and does not need slot 5. | `[C]:CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:1625-1645` -> `[C]:evm/src/core/BLSZKVerifierV2_1.sol:175-190`, `:262-272` (`_checkThresholdOnChain`), cache only in `:194-215` |
| F-S8-4 | `currentValidatorSetRoot = keccak256(abi.encode(sortedAddrs, sortedPowers, num, den))` commits addresses, powers and threshold, **not BLS keys**; `updateValidatorBLSKey` does not touch it. So "S9's keys are proven by S8" needs `validators[addr].blsPublicKey` (a `bytes` in storage: length word + data words) and the key guard `pubkeyBindingEnforced` + `authorizedPubkeyCommitments[pkc]` (the pkc used) - the Groth16 circuit places no constraint on which key signed (contract comment `:2223-2227`, and `:2164-2166`). The existing outcome evidence says the same: "the stated validator BLS keys are the ones the anchor registered ... not provable offline". | `[C]:CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:1714-1722,1754-1792,2223-2232`; `[V]:pkg/execution/outcome_evidence.go:52-54,326-329` |
| F-S8-5 | `identity-manifest.json` `storage[validatorList].elementSlotFormula` / `elementByteOffset` text is wrong (`floor(index*20/32)`, `(index*20)%32`). Solidity stores one 20-byte address per slot; the manifest's own `slotChecks` use `keccak256(13)+index` and live reads confirm it. | `[M]` builds `CertenAnchorV8_2/r5`.storage[validatorList]; `[M]` slotChecks formula `keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(13))) + 6`; live: M3 below (7 addresses at base+0..6 equal `validatorList(i)`) |
| F-S8-6 | Runbook F3 / dispatch text: account `owner` is `address(uint160(keccak256(adiURL)))` (not a constant) - already corrected in the manifest (RB12-B finding 11). Repeated here because the verification rule needs the `adiURL` **string slot** (slot 0) and the book **string slot** (slot 11), including the long-string form. | `[C]:CertenAccountV7_3.sol:138-145,250-251`; `[M]` account build immutables rules |
| F-S8-7 | Account storage that influences who may spend but is **absent from the manifest**: `_pageLevel`, `_pageLevelSet`, `_operationRequirements`, `_userRoles`, `_keyBooks`. [r3:S2-5] S8 now reads them: "the default level rule is code" was not the whole story (`_pageLevelSet` is tested before the governing-book test, `CertenAccountV7_3.sol:392-398`, and `_requiredLevelFor` reads `_operationRequirements`, `:661-678`), so step 14 proves the level from storage at N and the manifest carries the rows (item 11). V-MANIFEST classifies `_userRoles` and `_keyBooks` (not read by S8). | `[C]:CertenAccountV7_3.sol:237-246,392-399` |
| F-S8-8 (forwarded, outside S8) | The anchor ties the **outer** `BLSProofData.signedVotingPower/totalVotingPower` to the registry; the verifier's threshold test and the Groth16 public inputs use the **inner** blob's copies of the same two numbers; no code compares inner and outer. The key guard is the binding/commitment check, which is why S8 proves it at B_v. Route to contract review. | `[C]:CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:2181-2232` vs `[C]:BLSZKVerifierV2_1.sol:175-190,228-260` |
| F-S8-9 | S6's capture keeps evidence **in memory** until the L6 build (`ethproof.DefaultReplayGuards`, `replaycapture.go:655-658`) - a restart inside the minutes-long near-head window loses it. S8 capture must be durable at once (insert-only table, as S7 `proof_finality_capture`). | `[V]:pkg/ethproof/replaycapture.go:655-658`; `[V]:pkg/finality/capture.go:52`; `[V]:pkg/execution/outcome_evidence_build.go:240,332` |
| F-S8-10 (r2) | Attestation is unique by code: `usedCommitments[operationID]` is written once (`:1349`), never cleared, forced to `anchor.operationID` for batch anchors (`:2251-2253`); a recreated anchor record can never be executed again, so the block where it flips 0 -> 1 is THE attestation block. | `[C]:CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:856,894,1322,1349,2244,2251-2253`; M18 |
| F-S8-11 (r2) | Every writer of an authorization word is `onlyOwner` (anchor and verifier) except the two whose effect is the expected flip or which cannot touch a valid record; so the intra-block window is closed by "no execution as the owner in B_v" (rule IB), checkable from two owner account proofs and the block's transaction list. | `[C]:CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:1648-1904`, `BLSZKVerifierV2_1.sol:140,288,297`; M13, M15, M18, M19 |
| F-S8-12 (r2) | The settlement population is not one generation: 71 of 86 recent Sepolia settlements call selector `0x5b1264bc` (an older account generation, pinned neither by S6 nor by the manifest); no wrapper-contract settlement exists in 133 samples. | M12 |
| F-S8-13 (r2) | The owner of anchor and verifier on all four chains is one EOA `0x91C798AA...c059` (no code, non-zero nonce); the r1 text called it a "stated trust input", which `PROOF_V2` s.1 does not list - it is pinned and checked instead. | M13 |

### Q1. Exact container bytes (CFE1-style codec), contents, caps, size budget

**Answer.** A new strict binary container `CIE1` built from exactly the S7 primitives (`[S7]` s.0: big-endian integers, `lp()`, `STR`, `LIST`, `NODES` strictly ascending by keccak256 and unique, strict decode, `encode(decode(x)) == x`). It reuses `pkg/finality` `Writer`/`Reader`/`Limits` (`[V]:pkg/finality/codec.go:17-74`), so there is one codec to test. Full grammar: section "Proposed evidence structure". What is **in** it: full runtime code of every contract the verifier needs; one container-wide deduplicated `NODES` set holding all state-trie and storage-trie nodes (the verifier derives every read - address keys, slot keys, mapping slots, long-string data slots, `bytes` data slots - from the proven values and settlement facts; **no claimed query or value is carried**, as `[S7]` s.5.5 O2); the attestation transaction and receipt leaves; the attestation header and its parent header; the pinned owners' account proofs and the **full transaction list of the attestation block** (rule IB); the **hop headers** of the EIP-2935 hop chain (r2). What is **not** in it: the settlement header (it is `Settlement.Header`), any address other than the leg's `account`/`anchorId` (all others are *derived from proven storage*), any claimed slot value, the manifest, the S7 state root.

**Caps** (code constants of `DefaultLimits()` extended; raising one is a verifier release; exceeding ->`contract_identity_evidence_too_large{part,count,limit}`): container 4 MiB (`MaxReplayEvidenceBytes` precedent `[V]:pkg/ethproof/replaydecode.go:38`; measured typical 0.2 MB, 20x headroom); codes <= 16, each <= 262,144 B (`MaxCodeBytes`, `[V]:codec.go:43-50`); `NODES` <= 16,384, state/storage node <= 4,096 B (`MaxNodeBytes`), tx/receipt leaf <= 131,072 B (`max_attest_leaf_bytes`, dagger: the live attestation tx input is 2,660 B, M2); validators <= 64; `adiURL`/book string <= 1,024 B (<= 32 data words); attestation spine <= 4,096 headers (dagger; `max_attest_spine`); hop headers <= 16 (dagger; `max_attest_hops`); block transaction list <= 1 MiB and <= 4,096 transactions (dagger; `max_attest_block_txs_bytes`; measured typical 66.6 KB and maximum 121.5 KB on Sepolia, M15); provider failures <= 64 and each text <= 1,024 B (`MaxReplayProviderFailures`, `MaxReplayTextBytes`, `[V]:pkg/ethproof/redact.go:33,37`). Daggers are unmeasured round numbers, marked as `[S7]` s.8.2 marks them.

**Size budget per chain** (measured, M4; uncompressed; code does not compress usefully and is not compressed):

| chain | station S proofs (anchor 81 slots, verifier, generated, account, +factory) | code (anchor 24,337 + verifier 3,770 + generated 6,032 + account 14,562 + factory 24,306) | station V (pre+post anchor/verifier/generated accounts and the 81-slot set twice, 2935, tx+receipt, 2 headers) | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sepolia 11155111 | 31,086 B measured (+~4.4 KB factory) | 73,007 B | ~71 KB (tx/receipt part bounded, not measured) | ~180 KB |
| Base Sepolia 84532 | 35,809 B (+~4.1 KB) | 73,007 B | ~80 KB | ~193 KB |
| Arbitrum Sepolia 421614 | 30,849 B (+~4.2 KB) | 73,007 B | ~71 KB | ~179 KB |
| Adiri 2017 | 20,109 B (+~2.0 KB) | 73,007 B | ~51 KB | ~146 KB |

Citations: M4 below (script `sizes.mjs`, `eth_getProof` at head, 7 validators, `keyLen` 96). Factory and tx/receipt proof sizes are bounded from sibling measurements (account proofs 3,353-3,661 B, Adiri 1,304-1,355 B); WP-S8-3a/3b/3c measure them on first live capture (OQ-S8-4). r2 adds the block transaction list (Sepolia ~67-122 KB, the other chains < 20 KB, M15), two owner account proofs per state root (~7 KB each pair, estimate from the account-proof sizes above) and ~5 KB per hop (estimate); the Sepolia total therefore rises to about 300 KB, still far below the 4 MiB cap.

### Q2. WHEN and BY WHOM it is captured; static vs mutable; where it is stored and served

**Static vs mutable (what can be proven later vs only at the time).**

| fact | kind | provable later? | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| runtime code bytes, `codeHash`, immutables of anchor, verifier, generated verifier, account, factory | static | yes, from any later block whose state root a file can authenticate, **iff** the account existed at the leg block | code is proven directly at each block S8 judges (B_v-pre, B_v-post, N), so E1/E2 need **no** statement about SELFDESTRUCT or EIP-6780 (D11); that premise (EIP-6780, M10; per-chain activation, OQ-S8-2) matters only for the reserved later-static station. The only authenticated later state roots in a file are S7's spine blocks (`Covers`, `[S7]` s.5.2 step 5; Base/Arbitrum `l2Spine`; Adiri spine), and a public provider will not serve their state (R10 M8). So "later" needs an archive provider (OD4); **kind v1 captures static and mutable facts together** and a later-static station is reserved (OD-S8-11). |
| CREATE2 derivation of the account | static, arithmetic | yes, offline | needs the creation code (embedded in the verifier, hash-pinned by the manifest) |
| account `adiURL`, `governingBook` (slots 0, 11), anchor pointer (slot 2) | mutable only through `onlySelf` (pointer: `setAnchorContract`) | at the settlement block only | state root N |
| `anchors[anchorId]` (13 words), `isBatchAnchor`, `batchLeafCount` | mostly write-once (`valid` clearable by owner `invalidateAnchor`) | at N | what TX3 consulted |
| validator set root, thresholds, binding flag, authorized-commitment count/mapping, `validators[]` keys/powers, `blsZKVerifier`, enabled flag; verifier slots 0-2 | owner-mutable at any time | **only at B_v** (what TX2 judged) and at N (drift) | near-head `eth_getProof` windows (below) |
| EIP-2935 history slot for B_v | immutable once written | at N when N - B_v <= W, else along the hop chain (r2) | one storage proof per hop under the next header's stateRoot |

**WHEN.** Two capture events, both near head, both durable immediately:
- **E1 (attestation).** Trigger: the receipt of `executeComprehensiveProof` for the anchor (the submitter, `[V]:pkg/execution/batch_proof_submitter.go:26`) **and** the first sight of the anchor's `ProofExecuted(anchorId)` log by any other validator (all validators already read T = the attestation block, `batch_settlement_window.go:33`), whichever is first. Reads, at B_v and at B_v-1: the full AUTH slot set (the frozen table "AUTH slot set and writer premise", rows A01-A21, V01-V03, C01; r3 adds `isBatchAnchor`, `batchLeafCount` and, on a `manifest_history` row, the `pkcList` entries) [r3:S2-7] + `authorizedPubkeyCommitments[pkc]`, verifier slots 0-2, the account proofs of anchor, verifier, generated verifier **and of the pinned owner(s)** (rule IB); plus the tx and receipt of the attestation and **every transaction of B_v** (`blockTxs`). Keyed by `(chain, anchorId, block_hash, item)`, shared by every member leg of the batch.
- **E2 (settlement).** Trigger: first observation of the settlement receipt (same trigger as S6 capture: `CaptureReplayGuard`, `[V]:replaycapture.go:240`). Reads at the settlement block N: account, factory, anchor (record, auth slots), the EIP-2935 slot for B_v, the codes, and the authority-level slots of step 14 (`_pageLevelSet/_pageLevel[authorityBook][authorityPage]` and `_operationRequirements[selector]` per leg, derived from the decoded settlement calldata) [r3:S2-5]. The code bytes come from `eth_getCode` at N, hashed against the proven codeHash before they are stored (a provider's bytes are never kept unverified, as `proveAt`, `replaycapture.go:189-232`), plus the slot proof of the last hop at N.
- **E1b (hop ticks; r2, A5).** Trigger: block-height ticks, per chain, every <= floor(W/2) blocks from the first `ProofExecuted` of any unsettled anchor until every such anchor is settled or past `memberChainDeadline` (`[V]:pkg/execution/batch_orchestrator.go:1612`, the leaf `notAfter`). Each tick captures the tick block's header and the EIP-2935 slot proof of the previous tick (for the first tick after an attestation: of B_v) under the tick block's state root - always a head read, so provider proof windows never bite - durably and restart-safe (the next tick is derived from the last stored one). The assembled container carries the headers as `hopHeaders` (`link 1`). [r3.4:H8] Reach: the builder picks the fewest hops and consecutive ticks are <= floor(W/2) blocks apart, so the true reach is up to 16 x floor(W/2) + W (not (k+1) x W): on Base post-Denim (W = 27.3 min) about 4.1 h. One tick proves two things at once, the previous tick and B_v for every anchor still waiting, in ONE `eth_getProof` with several slots. The reach bound B_v + 16 ticks + W is an additional stop of the tick loop beside `memberChainDeadline`. [r3.6:H16] An anchor has several members, each with its own `memberChainDeadline` (the leaf `notAfter` of that member): the deadline of the tick loop for that anchor is the LATEST `memberChainDeadline` among its members that are still pending - after the earliest member's deadline the other members can still settle and must keep their hop ticks, and a member that has settled or is past its own deadline no longer counts. When no deadline is known (the bundle or its members cannot be read), the reach bound B_v + 16 ticks + W is the only stop. A tick whose stored predecessor was reorged away is stored with `Prev` 0 and the chain breaks (named `attest_block_out_of_reach` at assembly); equal-number forks are left to the verifier through the slot hash. A tick missed for more than W blocks breaks the chain for the anchors it served; those legs carry `attest_block_out_of_reach{gap,window,hops_carried,last_hop}` - the named, owner-acknowledged limit (Owner-gated list).

**BY WHOM.** The validator process that serves/stores the proof row, on the same path as the S6 capture and the S7 capture rows: a goroutine beside the observation that never blocks settlement, attestation or write-back and enters no hashed input (`replaycapture.go:26-31`). Every validator captures independently (cheap: one `eth_getProof` per contract per block with all slots in one call - M4 read 81 slots in one call on all four chains' public RPCs - plus the headers; no key material); the first complete capture wins per `(chain, anchorId, station)` in its own durable store. Which DB the proof service reads is OQ-S8-1.

**Provider windows per chain (measured by R10 on 2026-10-17, re-checked where marked) and what that forces:**

| chain | near-head proof window (public) | gap B_v -> N live | EIP-2935 | consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sepolia | Tenderly: depth <= 8-10 reliable (3/4 at 32, 0 at 64); publicnode: head only (8/8 at 0, 3/8 at 1) `[R10]` Q3 | 2 blocks (M1) | slot rule `B mod 8191`, canonical code `0x6e49e667...0a5d` (M5): covers 8191 x 12 s = 27 h | E1 must start within ~8 blocks (96 s) of B_v: capture is event-triggered, budget 2 min (`ReplayCaptureBudget`, `replaycapture.go:39`); a pre-state read at depth 1 needs Tenderly-class provider or the OD4 provider |
| Base Sepolia | `sepolia.base.org` reth with window: reliable to depth 2,000, OK 2,500-4,000 `[R10]` (pre-Denim; **post-Denim 200 ms blocks shrink the time window 10x - unmeasured**, OQ-S8-6); publicnode head only | 2 blocks | `B mod 8191`, same code (M5): 8191 x 0.2 s = 27 min post-Denim | settlements later than 27.3 min (measured, M14) after the attestation - an attester in window 0 is allowed 30 min, a takeover about 50 min - are outside one window and need the E1b hop chain |
| Arbitrum Sepolia | both public providers 6/6 to depth 100 (25 s at 4 blocks/s), 0-1/6 deeper `[R10]`; [r3.1:D1] measured again on 2026-10-23 (M31): ZAN `api.zan.top/arb-sepolia` served `eth_getProof` at 8.9M blocks of depth but returned `missing trie node` at another height only 1.1M blocks deep (availability is not monotonic in depth), Tenderly served headers, nonces and code at depth and refused `eth_getProof` (`maximum proof window`); the depth and rate-limit table is RE-MEASURED by WP-S8-3b before AT-9 and the OD4 sizing are accepted | 7 blocks (1.75 s) | **different code** (133 B, hash `0xceef1f6a...43ff`), slot rule `B mod 393168` (M5; matches on the live head): covers 27 h | E1 and E2 must run within ~25 s of the event: trigger on the receipt, not on a poll; OD4 provider strongly recommended |
| Adiri | public RPC head only (reth window 0) `[R10]` Q3; CERTEN's own node had window 1,209,600 (RB7, `[R11A]` OQ3, current state unknown) | 1 block | `B mod 8191`, same code (M5) | pre-state (depth 1) is **never** available publicly; Adiri capture needs CERTEN's own node (OQ-R11-3 in `[OQ]`); without it `contract_identity_unproven{part:authorization_attest, reason:attest_block_state_unavailable}` |

**WHERE stored and served (follows S6/S7 patterns, adds no hashed input):**
1. **Capture rows**, new insert-only table `proof_identity_capture(chain bigint, anchor_id bytea, block_hash bytea, item text, bytes bytea, created_at)` PK `(chain, anchor_id, block_hash, item)`; same triggers (UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE refused), same `Put` semantics (same bytes no-op, different bytes `ErrCaptureConflict`) as `[V]:pkg/finality/capture.go:52-60`; reuse `CheckCaptureItem`. Never read by a verifier.
2. **Final container**, new insert-only table `proof_contract_identity(proof_id uuid, seq bigint, chain bigint, block_number bigint, block_hash bytea, evidence bytea, evidence_sha256 bytea, digest bytea, created_at)` PK `(proof_id, seq)`, `octet_length` checks, same triggers. The served row is the greatest `seq`; a better capture later is a **new** row with `seq+1` (never an update), and a `Stated` container is refused when a captured one exists (`better_present`): the repository `Append` (the only write path) runs the S8 verifier at level `included` (everything except finality) and inserts only a container in which no part is in a refusal (R) state - unproven and pending parts are stored, they are facts about availability and finality; unavailability is **carried inside** the container as `Stated` parts (S6 pattern: the named state with providers' errors rides with the evidence) so a stored proof says why. A capture whose proofs are invalid (a lying provider) inserts nothing and is logged. Migration `<next free migration number at merge>_proof_contract_identity.sql` (00029 is also claimed by RB12-DBFIX, so no fixed number is written here; staged before the merge per the deploy-env rule).
3. **Serving**: a new member of the portable v2 document, composed at request time exactly like `finality`, `majors`, `govRootV3Inputs` (`[PS]:pkg/server/portable_handlers.go:130-137,215-248`, `finality_section.go:194`):
   `"contractIdentity": {"format":"certen-contract-identity/1","leg":{"chain","blockNumber","blockHash"},"evidence":"0x<container hex>","digest":"0x<hex32>"}` - absent (not empty) when the proof has none; `MaxContractIdentityBytes` guard like `MaxFinalityEvidenceBytes` (`portable_handlers.go:217-224`); the ETag includes the row identity. The member sits outside every hashed summary and outside govRoot v3/v4 and attestation inputs (`[V]:PROOF_V2.md` s.10.3). It is **not** an S7 addendum: the S7 chain is per level and append-only for finality levels (`[S7]` s.2.1-2.3); S8 is a fact set judged against S7's result, not a level.
4. **Digest** (storage consistency only, never authenticity, as `[S7]` s.2.6 states for D0): `digest = SHA-256( lp("certen:contract-identity:v1") || lp(D0) || lp(SHA-256(container)) )`, `D0 = finality.LegBinding(chain, number, blockHash)` (`[S7]` s.2.6, golden G1 reproduced independently in M6). The tag appears in exactly this one preimage. **Golden G-S8-0 (illustrative, M6; RB12 reproduces in Go and TS):** D0 = `1cea0a369d4a4167f9f3b9be09de1670dfb5718a866bbf7d2a6519b540643445`, evidence = ASCII `CIE1-test-vector`, `SHA-256(evidence)` = `3ead3c1527420fcc681037f621f0d9362ce452f3496162d92fd47ab5e23d6923`, preimage 103 bytes, **digest = `d7070fd59481084db1d6c97caf4cfb18865d4400a7a324a93799b39db7511edf`**.
   **Golden G-S8-1 (byte-exact container, M6b):** a fully `Stated` container for chain 11155111, leg (11845679, 32 x 0x22), zero codes, settle `Stated{reason capture_not_attempted_in_window}`, attest `Stated{reason attest_block_state_unavailable}`, each with `judgedBlock 11845679`, `judgedHash 32 x 0x22`, one provider failure (`rpc.example`, `no proof window`), empty detail, zero `NODES`: **379 bytes**, `SHA-256(container)` = `d009d115af904ed12afed394efb75040986863137151d6d1ef05494d36793937`, digest under the G1 D0 = `1102d40eacc348fce94b4995b4fe12f8b09e7770e4f7d7bdb972f4a9b58cd1d9`; hex (the reference for the codec):
   ``

**Legacy legs and named states.** (a) Legs settled by generations outside the manifest (V6/V6.1/V8.1 anchors, V7/V7_2 accounts and the older account generation behind selector `0x5b1264bc`, most of Sepolia's recent settlements, M12): the anchor/account code hash, if captured, is not a manifest row -> `contract_identity_unproven{part:code, address, reason:anchor_generation_unpinned | account_generation_unpinned, code_hash}`; the pins are never widened retroactively (manifest is append-only). (b) V8.2-era legs with no capture (settled before deployment of this feature, or capture missed): the proof row has no `contractIdentity` member; the verifier reports `contract_identity_unproven{part:all, reason:no_evidence_in_file}`; a missed capture inside the window is stored as a `Stated` container with `capture_not_attempted_in_window` / `state_unavailable` / `attest_block_state_unavailable` and the providers' failures (bounded, redacted: `BoundProviderText`, `[V]:replaycapture.go:150-166`). Stored v1/v2 verdicts never change (`00_STANDARD` s.2). (c) Public providers do not serve old proofs reliably (R10 M8; on Arbitrum Sepolia M31 shows that some providers serve some old heights and not others) [r3.1:D1], so a missed capture cannot be repaired later with any guarantee; the reserved later-static station (OD-S8-11) is the only way and needs OD4.

### Q3. Verification algorithm, level binding to S7, manifest embedding, S9 keys

Full ordered algorithm: section "Offline verification algorithm". Summary of the four sub-questions:

**Level binding.** The verifier takes the S7 result for the leg (`finalized_block{number,hash,stateRoot}` of `[S7]` R6, `V2_SPEC_S7.md:44`) and judges everything against `stateRoot(Settlement.Header)` read positionally (item 3; `[S7]` s.0). Output `judged_at_level` = the highest S7 level verified for that block; `state_root_authenticated` is **true only when S7 `finalized` is verified for exactly this block** (`finalized_block.hash == Leg.blockHash`). `l1_posted` does not authenticate a state root on Base/Arbitrum (`[S7]` s.1.1 quotes) so it never sets the flag. Status tokens (no weaker-shaped answer; the full six-row headline algebra is step 23): `verified` requires the flag **and no open part**; with all checks passing, the flag true and an open part, the headline is the distinct state `verified_core{open}`; with all checks passing but the flag false the headline is `pending` = `contract_identity_pending{level_reached, next_level:"finalized", reason:"state_root_not_authenticated"}` and the per-part table is still shown; S8 improves automatically when the S7 addendum appears (S8 evidence is immutable; no re-capture). Station V headers are authenticated **through** stateRoot(N) (EIP-2935 slot proof or a descending spine from N), so station V needs no S7 evidence of its own.

**Manifest embedding.** Mirrors S7 pins (`[V]:pkg/finality/pins.go:23-25`, `PinsSHA256` + `go:embed`; `[S7]` s.4.1): `evm/deployments/identity-manifest.json` in certen-contracts is the source; byte-identical LF copies at validator `pkg/contractidentity/manifest/identity-manifest.json` (`go:embed`) and SDK `packages/verify/src/proof-v2/identity/identity-manifest.json`; each verifier embeds `MANIFEST_SHA256` = `adc4c5438d...1e67` (the manifest's own rule: sha256 over the bytes with CRLF normalised to LF, `[M]` `manifestHash`) and refuses to start with `contract_identity_manifest_corrupt` if the embedded bytes hash otherwise; `.gitattributes` forces `eol=lf` for the three copies; CI job `identity-manifest-sync` compares the three copies and both constants; `--manifest <file>` overrides, the report states `manifest_source in {embedded, override:<sha256>, extension:<sha256>}`; an **extension** may only append rows and never alter, shadow or remove one - the allowed tables and the `manifest_shadow` refusal are in "Manifest v1.1 section list" item 7 (same rule as S7 s.4.3, tightened: an extension row can never override a `policy`, `eip2935`, `selectors` or `topics` key). Because the creation code is needed for the CREATE2 recomputation (OD-S8-3) the verifiers embed `evm/deployments/identity-bytecode/<Contract>.creation.bin`, each hash-pinned by the manifest's `builds[].creation.keccak` (`[M]` e.g. `CertenAccountV7_3/r5` creation 15,757 B).

**S9 keys proven by S8.** S9 supplies a `Registry9{members[(evmAddress, power, blsPublicKey bytes)], thresholdNumerator, thresholdDenominator, certenSetRoot}`: from the batch-outcome quorum (`OutcomeEvidence.Quorum.Validators/Threshold*`, `Anchor.CertenSetRoot`; note the builder reads these live from the anchor's own `validators(addr)` bytes, `[V]:pkg/execution/outcome_evidence_build.go:410-436`, so the byte encoding is the on-chain one) and/or from the intent quorum certificate's `ledger.BLSRegistryRecord` (`[V]:pkg/execution/intent_certificate_check.go:75-130`, `pkg/consensus/bls_registry.go:205` `RegistryCertenSetRoot`). Steps 18-21 prove, **at B_v**, that `validatorList` and every `validators[addr]` (registered, power, `bytes` key) equal `Registry9` member by member and in count, that the recomputed root `keccak256(abi.encode(sortedAddrs, sortedPowers, num, den))` equals the proven `currentValidatorSetRoot`, `Registry9.certenSetRoot` and the root inside the message the anchor accepted (step 20), and that the used `pkc` is authorized with binding enforced. Result: S9 may report its signer keys as "proven by S8". Without a `Registry9` in the file the registry link is the Open entry `not_checked{registry_link, no_registry_in_file}` unless the proven set root is in the manifest's `policy.setRootHistory` **and** the row also proves the keys (`keysDigest`) and the authorized set (`pkcCount`, `pkcList`) (then verified `via: manifest_history`; a row that cannot is the Open entry `not_checked{registry_keys,...}`, never `verified`) [r3:S2-1]; with a `Registry9` the link is a **core** part of the headline (step 21). The full proven registry (owner, root, threshold, members with keys, authorized-commitment count) is emitted in every report either way.

## Proposed evidence structure

Conventions are `[S7]` s.0 (`lp`, `STR`, `LIST<T>`, `B20/B32`, `u8/u32/u64` big-endian; strict decode; no trailing byte). Domain tag `certen:contract-identity:v1` appears only in the digest preimage (Q2 item 4). The container magic and kind are unchanged (`CIE1`, `contract-identity/v1`): nothing was published under r1, so the grammar below is the first one (golden G-S8-1 is regenerated in WP-S8-1 for r2 and supersedes r1's illustrative bytes; both are specification only until WP-S8-1 lands).

```
Container   = "CIE1"(4) || STR kind("contract-identity/v1") || u64 chain || Leg || LIST<Code> codes || Part settle || Part attest || NODES
Leg         = u64 blockNumber || B32 blockHash                 ; must equal the verified Settlement block (else block_mismatch)
Part        = u8 tag || ( tag 1: captured body        ; settle: empty body (every read is derived and sits in NODES); attest: Proof_attest
                        | tag 2: Stated )
Stated      = STR state("contract_identity_unproven") || STR reason || u64 judgedBlock || B32 judgedHash
              || LIST<ProviderFailure> || STR detail             ; informational, bounded, never judged as evidence
ProviderFailure = STR host || STR error
Code        = B20 address || LP runtime                     ; ascending by address, unique; shared by both parts (anchor, verifier, generated, account, factory)
Proof_attest = u8 link(0 same_block | 1 hops | 2 spine)
               || LP headerV || LP headerVParent                ; raw RLP, read positionally ([S7] s.0)
               || ( link 1: LIST<LP> hopHeaders )               ; ascending by number: X_1..X_k, k >= 0 (k = 0: EIP-2935 straight from N)
               || ( link 2: LIST<LP> spine )                    ; descending: h_0 hash == parentHash(Settlement.Header), h_k == headerV
               || u32 txIndex || LP txLeaf || LP receiptLeaf    ; consensus encodings; their proofs are in NODES
               || LIST<LP> blockTxs                             ; EVERY transaction of B_v in index order (typed wire encoding); r2, rule IB
NODES       = LIST<LP>  strictly ascending by keccak256(node), unique, shared by every proof of the container
```
- `blockTxs` (new, A3): the verifier rebuilds the ordered transaction trie (key `rlp(i)`), requires the root to equal `transactionsRoot(headerV)` and `blockTxs[txIndex] == txLeaf`; this authenticates the full transaction list of B_v from the same header that authenticates everything else. The nodes of that trie are **not** carried (the verifier rebuilds them from the list). Cap `max_attest_block_txs_bytes` 1 MiB and `max_block_txs` 4,096 (daggers; measured typical: Sepolia 66.6 KB average and 121.5 KB maximum over 24 sampled blocks, the other three chains < 20 KB, M15), a capture that meets a larger block stores the attest part as `Stated{block_too_large}` (the verifier reports `unproven{intra_block_window, reason: block_too_large{bytes,limit}}`), while a container above a cap is `evidence_too_large` at decode [r3:K].
- `hopHeaders` (new, A5): H_0 = `headerV`, H_1..H_k = `hopHeaders`, H_{k+1} = `Settlement.Header`; the proofs are in `NODES`. Cap `max_attest_hops` 16 (dagger; reach 17 x W: Base post-Denim 7.7 h). The spine (`link 2`) remains for chains whose history contract is absent and for the one-header case N - B_v = 1.
- Tag-1 `settle` is required for any `verified`; a `Stated` settle part yields `contract_identity_unproven{part:settle,...}` and the other part is still judged and reported (a missing code needed by a part is `unproven{code_not_carried}` for that part). `attest` link 0 is the case B_v == N (attestation and settlement in one block): `headerV` is then `Settlement.Header` and `headerVParent` its parent; the attestation transaction index must be **below** the settlement transaction's (step 16).
- The verifier derives and reads, per root, from `NODES`: account proofs for `keccak256(address)`; storage proofs for `keccak256(slot)`; absence as zero; the rules of S6 SPEC s.4c (`[V]:pkg/ethproof/testdata/s6replay1/SPEC.md` 4c) for empty storage roots, 32-byte value form and exclusion proofs. Tx/receipt leaves are proven at `rlp(txIndex)` under `transactionsRoot/receiptsRoot` of `headerV` (`ethproof.VerifyInclusion`, `[V]:pkg/ethproof/proof.go:114`; `VerifySettlement` shape `settlement.go:32-70`).
- Storage reads (all derived): account A at stateRoot(N): slot 0 string (+data), slot 2, slot 11 string (+data); factory F: slots `_deployedAccounts[account]` (base 2) and `_adiToAccount[keccak256(abi.encode(adiURL, book))]` (base 3); anchor: `anchors[anchorId]` = `keccak256(abi.encode(anchorId, 1)) + 0..12`, `isBatchAnchor` (base 2), `batchLeafCount` (base 3), `usedCommitments[operationID]` (base 18; r2), scalars 0, 5, 6, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 27, 29, 30, `validatorList[i]` = `keccak256(13)+i`, `validators[addr]` = `keccak256(abi.encode(addr, 12)) + 0..3` and the `bytes` key words at `keccak256(base+2) + j`, `authorizedPubkeyCommitments[pkc]` (base 4); verifier slots 0, 1, 2; owner accounts (rule IB; r2): the account proof (nonce, codeHash) of each pinned owner at `stateRoot_pre` and `stateRoot_post`; the EIP-2935 account `0x0000F90827F1C53a10cb7A02335B175320002935` and slot `B mod W` (W = 8191, Arbitrum 393168) for every hop. Slot arithmetic follows `[M]` `builds[].storage` **with the F-S8-5 correction (array element = base + index / itemsPerSlot, itemsPerSlot = floor(32 / elementBytes) = 1 for `address[]` and `bytes32[]`)**.
- Not carried and never trusted: codeHash/storageRoot/values declared by anyone; the container carries bytes only, every fact comes from a trie walk.

### Manifest v1.1 section list (WP-S8-0a-i / WP-S8-0a-ii [r3:S2-6c]; A9; schema string `identity-manifest/1.1`, new `manifestHash`, new `.sha256` file)
Append-only relative to d7e9c61 (no row of v1 is altered except the four defective text fields). Sections:
1. **Text corrections (D13/F-S8-5)** at all four places - `evm/deployments/README.md:334` (`floor(i * elementBytes / 32)` -> `floor(i / itemsPerSlot)`), `scripts/identity-manifest.mjs:279` (the generator emits `elementSlotFormula` and `elementByteOffset` from `floor(index * elemBytes / 32)` / `(index * elemBytes) % 32`; emit `keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(slot))) + floor(index / itemsPerSlot)` and `(index % itemsPerSlot) * elemBytes`), `evm/deployments/identity-manifest.json:445-446` (factory `address[]` at slot 4) and `:1030-1031` (`validatorList`, slot 13) - then regenerate the JSON from the script, never hand-edit. `slotChecks` already use `keccak256(13)+index` (live-verified in `[REV]` F-S8-5).
2. **`policy`**: `blsThreshold {2,3}`, `pubkeyBindingEnforced true`, `blsZKVerificationEnabled true`, `verifierThreshold {2,3}`, `minimumGovernanceLevel {min 1}`, `governanceVerifier 0x0` [r3:S2-3]; **`owner`** = per chain a history list of rows `{role: anchor|verifier, address, validFromBlock, validToBlock|null}` (initial rows: `0x91C798AA0Ad11d2670029b3B0572d154bd42c059` for both roles on all four chains, M13); optional **`setRootHistory`** rows `{chainId, root, validFromBlock, validToBlock|null, thresholdNumerator, thresholdDenominator, keysDigest, pkcCount, pkcList[]}` [r3:S2-1] (`keysDigest`, `pkcCount`, `pkcList` are defined byte-exactly in step 21c; the generator derives them from on-chain reads at row creation and `verify-identity-manifest.sh --onchain` re-derives them; a row without all three is valid JSON but can only produce the Open entry `not_checked{registry_keys}`); **`txScan`** per chain `{coveredTypes[], systemTypes[], evidence{<type>: {source, observation}}}` [r3:OQ-S8-10 / S2-7] [r3.1:D1] (`source` = the file:line at the pinned tag, `observation` = `{block, txHash, from, nonceBefore, nonceAfter}` or, for a `system` type, `{block, txHash, from, absent|nonceBefore==nonceAfter}`; the generator refuses a type in either list that lacks either half, and `--onchain` re-reads `nonceBefore` / `nonceAfter`): `coveredTypes` = types that run contract code as their `from` AND increment the nonce of `from` (so an execution as the owner changes `nonce(O)`); `systemTypes` = types that never run contract code (a transaction that runs no code changes nothing, whoever its `from` is: **there is no sender rule** - r2's was dropped because step 22 never applied it). [r3.1:D1] Final lists (ONE rule: a type is listed only with a pinned source AND an on-chain observation; the table "Transaction types per chain" holds both for every type): 11155111 covered 0x0 0x1 0x2 0x3 0x4; 84532 covered 0x0 0x2 0x4 0x7e; 421614 covered 0x0 0x2 0x4 0x65 0x66 0x68, system 0x64 0x69 0x6a; 2017 covered 0x0 0x2. Every other type (Base Sepolia 0x1, 0x3; Adiri 0x1, 0x3, 0x4; Arbitrum 0x1, 0x78) stays `U tx_type_unsupported`; the source line and the observation (or the reason that there is none) of every type is the table "Transaction types per chain" below (M23, M24, M29-M31); **`rules`**: the table "Policy rules" [r3:S2-3].
3. **`usedCommitments`** added to the F2 / AUTH table: the `storage` row exists (`CertenAnchorV8_2/r5` slot 18, M18); add it to `slotChecks` (key `operationID`) and name it in the authorization slot set.
4. **`eip2935`**: `{chain -> {address, codeHash, window, slotRule}}` four rows (M5: windows 8191 / 8191 / 393168 / 8191; code hashes `0x6e49e667...0a5d` and Arbitrum `0xceef1f6a...43ff`).
5. **`selectors` / `topics`**: `executeComprehensiveProof` `0x4ca9d0c8` (M2); account settlement selectors per generation (`CertenAccountV7_3`: `0x606f2c8d`, `0x329fe012`; `CertenAccountV7_2`: `0x57f8567d`, `0xb7daa901` as a named **not-pinned** generation row, so the verifier can name it); anchor-mediated settlement selectors treated as unsupported (`executeLegs`, `executeSingleLeg`: `CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:1182,1261`); topics `ProofExecuted` `0xaafab899...767d`, `LeafConsumed` `0xf65d4689...ea73`; **`topics.accountEvents`** [r3.1:D10] = `{GovernanceOperationExecuted: 0x74b66e509fa5263d4932860a2e1f6d187381ae68dee216710283b8677703ff12, GovernanceBatchExecuted: 0xcbcdc100c8089d25ab823b5044f746670e86a90b18c729bc7d27b7ce78733c56, LeafConsumed: 0xf65d46899882fe56bab13370dcd464db22e179625c161992c07d962286f7ea73}`, each the `cast keccak` of the canonical signature taken from the event declarations of `CertenAccountV7_3.sol:258-271` (`GovernanceOperationExecuted(string,address,uint256,bytes,uint8)`, `GovernanceBatchExecuted(string,bytes32,uint256,uint8)`, `LeafConsumed(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32)`; the enum `AuthorityLevel` is `uint8`), read by the step 3 `not_applicable` row and by step 14 (M33). **`generations`** (new in this item): rows `{role: account|anchor|blsZkVerifier, generation, pinned:false, kind: catalogued|observed, maskedKeccak, runtimeBytes, references, source}` [r3:S2-6c] (`observed` rows: item 12) for every older build any CERTEN factory or anchor deployment put on the four chains (accounts V4-V7_2 from `evm/src/account/**` including `Archive-legacy`, anchors V6-V8.1 from `evm/src/core/**`), derived by the same generator from the archived sources; with a **completeness check** in `--onchain`: every account announced by `AccountDeployed` on each historical factory, and every anchor in `evm/deployments/**`, has a masked hash in `builds` or `generations`, else the manifest build fails. This is what lets the verifier tell an older legitimate generation (`U ..._generation_unpinned`) from code in no row (`R code_not_published`) without ever widening a pin.
6. **Creation artifacts**: `evm/deployments/identity-bytecode/<Contract>.creation.bin` for the account build (the only creation code the verifier needs, for the CREATE2 recomputation of step 8) and, so that a reviewer can re-derive every build, for all seven builds, each pinned by `builds[].creation.keccak` plus a sha256 in a new `creationArtifacts` table; the directory does **not** exist at d7e9c61 (M16) - WP-S8-0a-i creates it from the recorded builds and `verify-identity-manifest.sh` re-derives each file.
7. **Extension rule (forbid shadowing)**: an extension (`--manifest` extension form) may add rows to `builds`, `deployments`, `accounts`, `eip2935`, `chains` and `policy.txScan` (rows for NEW chain ids only), `generations`, `policy.owner`, `policy.setRootHistory` (new rows only, `validFromBlock` after the last row of that key; an appended row retires the earlier row of the same key at its own `validFromBlock` - 1 [r3.6:H13]: the earlier row is kept as stored, and the last block it is valid at is the smaller of its stored `validToBlock` (when it has one) and the new row's `validFromBlock` - 1, so a stored `validToBlock` that already ends earlier wins and is never extended, and an open row ends at the new row's `validFromBlock` - 1; a row whose `validToBlock` is before its own `validFromBlock` is refused, in the base and in an extension (`contract_identity_manifest_corrupt` in Go; the CI tooling refuses it as `validToBlock must not be before validFromBlock`), and a row with `validToBlock` = `validFromBlock` is valid at exactly that block), and nothing else [r3.2:E-e]. A NEW chain id (a `chains[]` row that is not in the base) needs ALL its dependent rows in the same extension - `eip2935[chain]`, `policy.txScan[chain]`, `policy.owner` rows of both roles and `deployments` rows of the five roles whose `build` exists - else the refusal `contract_identity_manifest_unknown{chain}`; a dependent row for a chain that is in neither the base nor the extension's `chains` is the same refusal [r3.2:E-e]. It may **never** redefine a primary key already present (`builds[contract/variant]`, `deployments[chainId,role]`, `eip2935[chainId]`, `policy.blsThreshold`, `policy.pubkeyBindingEnforced`, `policy.blsZKVerificationEnabled`, `policy.verifierThreshold`, `policy.minimumGovernanceLevel`, `policy.governanceVerifier`, `policy.rules`, `policy.txScan[chainId]`, `chains[chainId]`, `generations[role,maskedKeccak]` [r3.2:E-e][r3.2:E-e2: the pair (role, generation) is NOT unique - CertenAccountV7 has a catalogued and an observed row, and several `unidentified` families exist - while a masked runtime hash identifies the code], `selectors`, `topics`). A collision is the refusal `contract_identity_manifest_shadow{table,key}`; the report carries `manifest_source` and, for an extension, its sha256. [r3.6:H14] **Canonical spelling of a hex key.** A 32-byte hex value that is (part of) a primary key - today only `generations[].maskedKeccak` - has exactly one spelling: `0x` followed by exactly 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits. The key of a row is that string itself (`role,maskedKeccak`); it is never lower-cased, trimmed or otherwise repaired. A row spelled otherwise (upper-case or mixed-case digits, `0X`, no prefix, another length, surrounding white space, empty) is refused as `contract_identity_manifest_corrupt` (the cause names the row), in the embedded or an override manifest and in an extension, before any shadow test: an upper-case copy of an existing key is `manifest_corrupt`, not `manifest_shadow`. The 16 `generations` rows of the embedded manifest are canonical (checked at r3.6), so the manifest and its pin are unchanged. A lookup (`GenerationFor`) still compares its argument case-insensitively; that cannot change a verdict because every stored key is canonical. The CI tooling (`scripts/lib/extension.mjs`) lower-cases before it compares and can therefore accept a spelling that Go refuses; Go is authoritative. The other 32-byte hex values of the manifest (`root`, `keysDigest`, `pkcList`, code hashes) are values, not keys. [r3.6:H15] **Names and reach of the dependents check.** The refusal strings are `contract_identity_manifest_unknown{chain}` and `contract_identity_manifest_shadow{table,key}`; the vocabulary table (Item 3), the vector rows (Item 5) and the review matrix write them without the common prefix `contract_identity_` (`manifest_unknown`, `manifest_shadow`): one code each (`CodeManifestUnknown`, `CodeManifestShadow` in `names_gen.go`). The dependents rule above is judged on the MERGED manifest as a whole, not only on the rows the extension adds: every dependent row of the merged tables (`deployments`, `accounts`, `eip2935`, `policy.txScan`, `policy.owner`, `policy.setRootHistory`) belongs to a chain of the merged `chains[]`, and every chain that is not in the base has all its dependent rows; the refusal carries the smallest chain id found foreign, else the smallest incomplete new chain. Go (`checkChains`) is authoritative. The CI tooling checks the rows the extension adds against the merged `chains[]`, and the completeness of each new chain: a subset check run in CI that, for the chain rules, cannot accept an extension that Go refuses (every dependent row of the pinned base belongs to a base chain); its acceptance is not a verifier verdict.
8. **CI**: `identity-manifest-sync` (three copies, two constants) and `verify-identity-manifest.sh` extended to the new sections (offline re-derivation of `eip2935` code hashes is not possible offline: `--onchain` checks them live, as it does for deployments).
9. **`authSlots`** [r3:S2-7]: the "AUTH slot set" table below (rows A01-A21, V01-V03, C01) in machine form, one JSON row per table row; the generator checks each row's slot, byte offset and type against `forge inspect <contract> storageLayout` of the same build and fails on a mismatch.
10. **`builds[].authWriters`, `authReads`, `authWriterAllowList`, `authExempt`** [r3:S2-7 / M18]: recorded by the generator from the solc AST of the two builds `CertenAnchorV8_2/r5` and `BLSZKVerifierV2_1/r5`, exactly as "AUTH slot set and writer premise" specifies; `verify-identity-manifest.sh` fails the manifest build on any of its six conditions, restated at member granularity in the mechanical premise [r3.1:D5]; the item also records the per-contract `ownerModifier` pins (body hash, predicate, owner slot) and the `guard` (text, key identifier, guarded paths) of each allow-listed creation function; rule IB (step 22) is valid only for a build whose `authWriters.status` is `pass` and whose allow-list is a subset of the verifier's frozen allow-list. Reference implementation of the extraction and of the gate (prototype at member level, with `design/vectors/s8/negctl/`: an honest contract that passes and 16 seeded defects that each fail exactly the stated condition): `design/vectors/s8/authwriters.mjs` with the policies `authwriters.policy.{CertenAnchorV8_2,BLSZKVerifierV2_1}.json` [r3.1:D5]; the variable-level r3 prototype and its outputs are kept as `authwriters.varlevel.mjs` and `authwriters.*.d7e9c61.varlevel.json`.
11. **Account storage rows** [r3:S2-5]: `storage` rows for `_operationRequirements` (slot 8, key `bytes4` right-padded), `_pageLevel` (9) and `_pageLevelSet` (10) (two-level mapping: `keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(page), keccak256(abi.encode(book, uint256(slot)))))`) plus `slotChecks` that read the six constructor defaults `_operationRequirements[...]` (`CertenAccountV7_3.sol:704-709`) live; verified by `design/vectors/s8/SlotProbe.t.sol` (M21). This closes F-S8-7 ("V-MANIFEST must classify them").
12. **`generations` row kinds** [r3:S2-6c]: `catalogued` (the family's source and settings are reproducible: the generator builds it, the masked hash is derived) and `observed` (the family exists on a chain - announced by `AccountDeployed` of a historical factory or an anchor in `evm/deployments/**` - but its source or compile settings cannot be reproduced bit-exactly: the row is created by `--onchain` from `cast code`, carries `{kind:"observed", maskedKeccak, runtimeBytes, evidence:[{chainId,address,block,codeHash}], sourceReason}` and `references` computed from the on-chain bytes where the unmasked bytes are compared against `catalogued` neighbours, else empty). An `observed` row can never be referenced by `builds`, a `policy` row, `selectors` or any pin; the completeness check passes when every announced family is `catalogued` or `observed`, so a family that cannot be reproduced no longer fails the manifest CI forever and no hash enters unnamed.

Words read on the attestation path (the transitive closure of `executeComprehensiveProof`, AST, M20) that are **not** in the table: `usedNonces` (slot 19) only. It is *restrict-only*: its single reader is `nonceValid = !usedNonces[...]` (`CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:2002`) and its single writer assigns the literal `true` (`:1352`), so no state of it can make an otherwise rejected attestation accept; the generator re-checks both facts mechanically (`authExempt`, condition (e) below) and the report lists it under `rules_not_judged`.

**Mechanical premise [r3:S2-7 / M18] [r3.1:D5] (member level).** The manifest generator records, for the two builds `CertenAnchorV8_2/r5` and `BLSZKVerifierV2_1/r5`, from the forge artifact (`--ast --extra-output storageLayout`, the generator's own build command `scripts/identity-manifest.mjs:205`): (1) *entry points* = constructor, receive, fallback and every public/external function of the most-derived contract and its bases; (2) per entry point E the *closure* = E, its modifiers, every internal function reachable through calls (virtual dispatch to the most-derived override; `super.f()`), with the direct effects read from the AST: *writes* = the **member path** that is written - the state variable at the root of the left side of an assignment, of `++`/`--`/`delete`, or the receiver of `.push`/`.pop`, followed by the index steps (`[]`) and struct-member steps (`.member`) down to the written value, resolved through the build's `storageLayout` types to (variable, base slot, struct word, byte offset, bytes, whole-record flag) - for example `anchors[].governanceExecuted @1+10:22` (slot 1, struct word 10, byte 22) and `anchors[]` for the whole-record assignment `anchors[id] = Anchor({...})`; a local `storage` pointer is resolved to the path of its single initialiser; *hazards* = `delegatecall`, `callcode`, `selfdestruct`, assembly `sstore`/`create`/`create2`/`delegatecall`/`callcode`/`selfdestruct`, **any call whose callee is not a direct reference to a function, modifier, event, error or builtin** (a function-typed variable, parameter or struct member, an element of an array of function pointers, the result of a call, a conditional: `indirect_call`), **any function type declared in the contract** (`function_type_declared`) [r3.2:D14], **any write the extractor cannot attribute to a member path** (a storage pointer that is a parameter or a return value, comes from a function call or a conditional, is declared without an initialiser or is assigned more than once; a tuple or call result used as the root of an lvalue; an index or member step the layout cannot resolve), and the reassignment of a function parameter in a function that carries a guard; *reads* = state variables referenced in a non-writing position (variable granularity suffices for reads); (3) `authWriters[E] = {signature, visibility, modifiers, callees (the transitive internal functions and modifiers), writes:[{variable, path, slot, word, offset, bytes, whole, key, assigned}], hazards}` for every E whose writes meet the AUTH variables, and `authReads` = the reads of the closure of `executeComprehensiveProof`; (4) `ownerModifier` = per contract `{contract, modifier:"onlyOwner", bodyHash, predicate:"msg.sender == owner", shape, ownerSlot}`, where `bodyHash` is the lowercase hexadecimal sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes of `JSON.stringify(C(body))` (no whitespace), `body` being the `Block` node of the modifier in the compact JSON AST that solc 0.8.24 emits (the `ast` member of the forge artifact built with `--ast`) and `C` defined by cases [r3.2:D13]: an array becomes the array of `C` of its elements; a JSON object becomes an object that omits every key in `id src scope referencedDeclaration typeDescriptions typeIdentifier typeString argumentTypes overloadedDeclarations documentation isPure isLValue lValueRequested isConstant hexValue functionReturnParameters canonicalName baseFunctions commonType absolutePath nodes` and every key whose name ends in `Location` or `Locations` (`nameLocation`, `nameLocations`, `memberLocation`: they carry the source-unit index), holds every other key with `C` of its value in ascending UTF-16 code-unit order of the key, and, when the original object has `nodeType` `Identifier` and a `referencedDeclaration`, also holds the key `ref` = the string `<nodeType>:<name>` of the declaration node with that id (any source unit of the same compilation) followed by `:state` when that node has `stateVariable` true, or the string `builtin` when no node has that id (the negative ids of `msg`, `require`, `revert`); any other value stays as it is. No node id, source range, source-unit index or type string takes part, so the hash does not depend on which sources are compiled together (it depends on the compiler version). The same text is in `evm/deployments/README.md` ("The owner-modifier body hash"); `scripts/tests/onlyowner-hash.independent.mjs` re-computes the pins from that text alone with no shared code. `predicate` is recognised from two accepted shapes only: `if (!(P)) revert E(); _;` and `require(P, "msg"); _;` with `P` = `msg.sender == owner` (either operand order, `owner` the contract's own state variable). The anchor's modifier (`CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:653-656`, `if (!(msg.sender == owner)) revert OnlyOwner(); _;`) and the verifier's (`BLSZKVerifierV2_1.sol:140-143`, `require(msg.sender == owner, "Only owner"); _;`) have different bodies and are two DIFFERENT pinned entries (anchor body hash `2235ebcaad22d313643d18fd46bb4a2ffe4bb87888cff6bd9e4c9de513d21f2d`, verifier `e1694b57d85b9a770c1ae014c0e6f69bac4cbd2c2fca86a32c2d4f4fe3689309`, reproduced from the generator's own six-source build and from a three-source build by the library and by the independent implementation) [r3.2:D13]; a modifier named `onlyOwner` whose body hash is not the pinned one of its contract fails the build. `verify-identity-manifest.sh` **fails the manifest build** when: (a) any entry has a hazard (this includes an unattributable write); (b) an entry whose writes meet an AUTH variable has no pinned `onlyOwner` among its modifiers and is not in `authWriterAllowList`; (c) an allow-listed entry writes an AUTH **member** outside its `allowedWrites` (member granularity: a whole-record write is allowed only when the whole-record path is listed), or its pinned `guard` does not verify - the first statement of the function must equal the guard text after whitespace normalisation, and every write of the guarded paths must be keyed by the guard's key identifier, which must be a function parameter that the function never reassigns; (d) the `onlyOwner` of a contract with AUTH writers is not its pinned `ownerModifier` entry (body hash, predicate, owner slot); (e) `authReads` contains a state variable that is neither an AUTH variable nor in `authExempt`, or an `authExempt` variable has a write that assigns anything but the literal `true`; (f) `owner` is written outside the constructor and `transferOwnership`. The **frozen IB allow-list** (data; each row is the guard citation of the writer table above): `constructor` (deployment only: it runs once, in the creation transaction, which cannot be the attestation block of a record created after it); `createAnchor` -> `anchors[]` (whole record); `createBatchAnchor` -> `anchors[]`, `isBatchAnchor[]`, `batchLeafCount[]`; both under the guard `if (!(!anchors[bundleId].valid)) revert AnchorAlreadyExists();` as first statement with key identifier `bundleId` (`CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:714` and `:856`); `executeComprehensiveProof` -> `anchors[].proofExecuted` (@1+10:21), `anchors[].governanceLevel` (@1+10:23), `usedCommitments[]` (@18) (and the exempt `usedNonces`); `executeWithGovernance` -> `anchors[].governanceExecuted` (@1+10:22) and nothing else. **The frozen allow-list is a constant of the verifier (Go and TS), not only a manifest field.** Rule IB is valid only for a build row whose `authWriters.status` is `pass` AND whose `authWriterAllowList` is a subset of the verifier's frozen allow-list; otherwise the verifier refuses to apply it: `U intra_block_window{reason:build_without_writer_proof, build, condition}` with `condition` in {status_missing, a, b, c, d, e, f, allowlist_not_frozen}. A later build row (V8_3) is rule-IB-verified only through its own AST and the hazard classes above [r3.2:D14] (it inherits nothing from this build): a new non-owner function that writes an AUTH member, or an allow-listed function that writes one more member (say `anchors[].valid`), fails (b) / (c) in its own AST, and an allow-list that a manifest author widens is caught by `allowlist_not_frozen` until a verifier release extends the frozen list. The one thing that is not proven by the build itself is named as a residual (R-WRITERS, Trust base), not promised away.

**Policy rules** (manifest `policy.rules`, [r3:S2-3]; the executed ids are printed as `rules_judged`, the AUTH rows and exempt words that no rule judges as `rules_not_judged` with a reason):

| rule id | AUTH rows | predicate | at | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PAUSED | A01 | `== 0` | pre, post | `R authorization_mismatch{field:paused}` (a successful attestation implies not paused; paused at both boundaries contradicts the receipt) |
| BINDING | A08 | `== 1` | pre, post | `R authorization_mismatch{field:binding}` |
| ENABLED | A19 | `== 1` | pre, post | `R authorization_mismatch{field:enabled}` |
| THRESHOLD-A | A12, A13 | `== policy.blsThreshold` | pre, post | `R authorization_mismatch{field:threshold}` |
| THRESHOLD-V | V01, V02 | `== policy.verifierThreshold` | pre, post | `R authorization_mismatch{field:verifier_threshold}` |
| OWNER | A16, V03 | in a `policy.owner` row covering B_v | pre, post | `R authorization_mismatch{field:anchor_owner or verifier_owner}` |
| GOVVERIFIER | A17 | `== 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` | pre, post | `U governance_verifier_unpinned{address,at}` |
| MINGOV | A20 | `>= policy.minimumGovernanceLevel.min` (1) | pre, post | `R authorization_mismatch{field:minimum_governance_level}` |
| SETROOT | A14 and A09-A11 | recomputed root equals A14 | post (pre equal) | `R authorization_mismatch{field:set_root}` |
| VERIFIER-ID | A18 | a `[MAN]` `blsZkVerifier` row | pre, post | steps 12 / 19a |

**Verdict precedence of every rule above [r3.1:D4].** Each rule (and every other `R authorization_mismatch` / `commitment_not_authorized` of steps 19 and 21b) is evaluated on the two attest stations, pre and post, and "pre, post" in the table means *both stations are read*, not "either". The verdict is **`R` only when ALL of the following hold**: (1) the word is **equal** at pre and post, (2) the predicate **fails at both** stations, and (3) rule IB (step 22) is `verified` for B_v - it shows that no transaction of B_v executed as the owner, so the word cannot have been changed and restored inside the block and the state that violates the rule is the state the attestation was judged under. **Otherwise the verdict is `U`, never `R`:** (a) the word differs between pre and post - including a violation at only ONE station (the owner changed the word in B_v, before or after the attestation) - gives `U authorization_attest{reason:state_changed_in_block{field,pre,post,block}}` (step 18); (b) the word is equal and fails at both stations but the owner was active in B_v gives `U intra_block_window{reason:owner_active_in_block{address,pre,post}}` on the part `intra_block_window`, and the part `authorization_attest` carries the same `U` code (`owner_active_in_block`); (c) the word is equal and fails at both stations and IB is `U` for another reason (`owner_not_eoa`, `tx_type_unsupported`, `block_too_large`, `build_without_writer_proof`) gives the part `authorization_attest` the `U` code of that IB state. A violation is therefore reported as a refusal only when it was the real state of the whole block and the owner provably did not touch it.

Not judged, with the reason printed: A21 (`minimumGovernanceLevelForValueOps` is read only by `executeWithGovernance`, `CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:1398`, not on the attestation path; reported in `registry`), `usedNonces` (restrict-only, above), A09 word 3 `registeredAt` (informational; no acceptance decision reads it), slot 28 `operators` (not read by the attestation path). A `governanceVerifier` that is non-zero is **never pinned in v1**: `_verifyGovernanceProof` hands the decision to that contract when slot 29 is non-zero (`:2067-2078`) and S8 has no semantics for it, so the verdict is `U governance_verifier_unpinned` whatever the address; a manifest row for it would be designed against an artifact that does not exist (live value: zero on all four anchors, M22) - a judged `GovernanceVerifier` build is a `contract-identity/v2` item.

**Transaction types per chain [r3:OQ-S8-10] [r3.1:D1] [r3.1:D7]** (rule IB2). **ONE rule for every chain and every type.** A type is `covered` (runs contract code as its `from` AND increments the nonce of `from` unconditionally, so an execution as the owner changes `nonce(O)`) or `system` (never runs contract code, so whoever its `from` is, it changes nothing) **only with BOTH** (i) a *source citation* (file:line at the pinned tag of the chain's client, or of the protocol specification) showing that the type either runs no contract code or increments the sender nonce unconditionally, AND (ii) at least one *on-chain observation* of a transaction of that type: block, transaction hash and the `from` nonce at N-1 and at N (`cast nonce <from> --block <N-1|N>`; on Arbitrum also proven with `eth_getProof` under the header `stateRoot`), or, for a `system` type, the `from` absent (or its nonce unchanged) at N-1 and at N. A type with a source but no observation, or an observation but no source, is `tx_type_unsupported` (a named `U`); **nothing is assumed**, and every type that was looked for is in the table. Pinned sources: Arbitrum Sepolia = Nitro tag v3.11.3 (commit 4130f4c5, go-ethereum fork f3a966e6), ArbOS 61 = `arbOSVersion()` 116 (M23); Sepolia = `ethereum/execution-specs` tag v2.20.0 (commit 2004296f2ffc), `src/ethereum/forks/osaka/`; Base Sepolia = `base/base` tag v1.5.0 (commit e0fe7fa0bef1; the public endpoint reports `reth/v2.5.2-7134be3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/base/v1.5.0`, M30) with revm-handler 42.0.1 (crates.io); Adiri = `telcoin-network` `d72cc2bc` (tag `v0.16.0-adiri`, the commit every public endpoint reports, `[R11A]`) with revm-handler 15.0.0 (`Cargo.lock:10445-10446` of that commit). Observations: M29 (Arbitrum), M30 (the other three chains); scripts `design/vectors/s8/{arbtypes,arbscan,typeobs}.mjs`. The manifest `txScan` carries the source and the observation of every type it lists (item 2), and `verify-identity-manifest.sh --onchain` re-reads every observation.
