## Offline verification algorithm

Labels: **[S6]** the settlement already verified by S6 (`VerifySettlement`: header, tx leaf, receipt status/logs) and its replay-guard check; **[S7]** S7 result for the leg; **[MAN]** manifest (embedded, hash-checked); **[C]** standard cryptography and the trie rules; **[CHAIN]** contract behaviour as given by the *pinned build* (conclusions of the form "the pinned code can only have done X"). Each step names its refusal; the first failing step of a part decides that part; parts are independent, the report lists all. **Result classes** (used by every step): *R* = refused (a mismatch is proven), *U* = `unproven{...}` (the evidence cannot establish it), *Open* = `alert` / `drift` / `not_checked` (reported, bars `verified`, does not bar `verified_core`), see "Headline algebra" (step 23).

Conventions of the steps: storage byte offsets are counted from the **least-significant** end of the 32-byte word, as Solidity packs and as `[M]` `byteOffset` states: byte `b(i)` is `word[31 - i]` (`anchors[id]` word 10 = `validator`(bytes 0-19) `valid`(20) `proofExecuted`(21) `governanceExecuted`(22) `governanceLevel`(23), bytes 24-31 zero; measured in M9); a mapping slot is `keccak256(abi.encode(key, base))`, an array element `keccak256(abi.encode(base)) + floor(index / itemsPerSlot)` (itemsPerSlot = 1 for `address[]`), `bytes`/`string` as in step 6. [r3.1:D2] [r3.1:D3] **Vocabulary rule:** the field `at` of any state is one of `settle`, `attest_pre`, `attest_post` (Freeze item 4), never `attest`; a predicate evaluated at both attest stations reports the first station at which it fails, pre before post. **`proof_invalid`:** every proof read of steps 5-22 (each account, slot, string, `bytes`, hop and EIP-2935 read) whose trie walk does not verify against its root raises `R proof_invalid{root,address,slot}` with `root` in {settle, attest_pre, attest_post, hop:`<i>`}; this sentence is the single raise of that registry row. **Roles:** `role` values are the manifest spellings (Freeze item 4): `anchor`, `blsZkVerifier`, `groth16Verifier` (the generated Groth16 verifier `G`), `accountFactory`, `outcomeRegistry` (the five `deployments[].role` values) and `account`, `owner`.

Inputs: `LegContext{Settlement, Tx, Receipt, ADIURL (member), S6Status in {s6_proven, s6_silent, s6_not_proven} [r3.1:D12] (+ `S6Reason` for `s6_silent`, `S6State` for `s6_not_proven`), S6 {Contract, Slot.Key, SettlementBlock, ProvenAt, CodeHash} (mandatory when `S6Status == s6_proven`; `StateRoot` removed [r3:S2-4 iii]), Batch {batchRoot, batchOperationID, accSetRoot, incarnation} (all four mandatory, non-zero), Registry9 (optional; with SignerCommitment), S7 report (mandatory)}`, container bytes, manifest (the exact field table with the refusal each mandatory field raises is "Freeze inventory" item 2). `anchorId` is not an input: it is `topic1` of the selected `LeafConsumed` log (step 3b) [r3:S2-4 i]. `authorityBook`, `authorityPage` and the legs' `(target, value, selector)` are read from the settlement calldata (step 14), not supplied [r3:S2-5].

0. **Manifest.** Embedded bytes hash to `MANIFEST_SHA256` else `contract_identity_manifest_corrupt` (refuse to start). `chains[]` has `Settlement.chainId` else `contract_identity_manifest_unknown{chain}`. An extension that redefines a primary key of v1.1 -> `contract_identity_manifest_shadow{table,key}`. [MAN]
1. **Decode** strictly (`[S7]` s.0): magic, kind `contract-identity/v1` (else `contract_identity_evidence_unrecognised{kind,version}`), counts <= caps (`evidence_too_large{part,count,limit}`), `NODES` ascending/unique, no trailing byte (`evidence_malformed{part,index,reason,got_len,want_len}`) [r3.1:D2: the names of the registry, word for word]; `encode(decode(x)) == x`.
1b. **Context (A2).** `Batch` carries all four non-zero values and the S7 report is present, else `contract_identity_context_incomplete{missing:[...]}` (R, framework class: the proof file always carries these, so a missing one is an integration error, never an attribute); a PRESENT `Registry9` that has no members, a key that is not 192 lowercase hex characters or a `0x` prefix is `missing:[registry9]`, and `LegContext.Chain` zero is part of the token `settlement` [r3.2:E-g]. If `S6Status == s6_proven`, `S6` is present (same refusal); `s6_silent` (S6 made no claim) and `s6_not_proven` (S6 judged the leg and did not prove it; `S6State` non-empty) are valid, explicit values (step 3 row table), a forgotten field is not [r3:S2-4] [r3.1:D12].
1c. **Presence of the container and of its parts [r3.1:D3].** (a) *No container* (the proof file has no `contractIdentity` member, or the caller passes none): `U unproven{part:all, reason:no_evidence_in_file}`; the headline is `unproven`, steps 2-24 do not run, and the report lists every judged part as `unproven` with this reason (steps 0 and 1b still ran, so the manifest and the context are judged). (b) *`settle` part `Stated{reason}`* (reasons `capture_not_attempted_in_window`, `state_unavailable`; the carried `judgedBlock`, `judgedHash` and provider failures ride in the state): every judged part that needs a read at the settlement block is `U unproven{part:<that part>, reason:<the carried reason>}` - `code_identity` (5, 10, 12), `account_provenance` (6-8), `pointer` (9), `record` (11), `authority_level` (14), `state_at_settlement` (13) - and so is the generation identification of step 3(e); steps 3(a)-3(d) (they read only the receipt and the calldata), step 4 when `S6.ProvenAt.hash == Leg.blockHash` (otherwise `s6_link` is `U` with the carried reason), and every attest part (15-22, 21) are still judged from their own evidence. (c) *`attest` part `Stated` or absent* is step 15 (`attest_block_state_unavailable`, `attest_block_out_of_reach`, `attest_event_not_found`, `block_too_large`, `capture_not_attempted_in_window`, `state_unavailable`). A `Stated` part can never raise a status above `unproven` (vector VS8-181). **Carried reasons [r3.2:E-f]:** a `Stated` part whose reason is not one of the six builder reasons (Item 4, 'Stated reason (builders)') is refused by the verifier, whichever step reads it first (1c(b) for `settle`, 15 for `attest`), as `evidence_malformed{part:<settle|attest>,reason:unknown_stated_reason}` (framework class, headline `refused`); decode checks the syntax `[a-z0-9_]{1,64}` only, the closed list is a verifier rule like `nodes_unreferenced`. [r3.2:F7] When the `settle` part is `Stated`, steps 15-22 (step 21 included: its verifier facts are settle reads) are still judged from their own evidence and from context-derived inputs only (`anchorId` from the `LeafConsumed` log of the receipt, the batch facts, the manifest pins); a step that would need a fact that only a settlement-block read supplies decides its part `U` carrying the Stated settle reason, never a silent skip.
2. **Leg.** `Leg.blockNumber/blockHash` equal the verified Settlement block (number read positionally, `keccak256(header) == blockHash`) and `chain` equals the catalogue chain: else `contract_identity_block_mismatch{field,want,got}`. [S6]
3. **Settlement facts and path (A7).** (a) Receipt status 1 else `U settlement_not_executed`. (b) Select the `LeafConsumed(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32)` logs of the receipt (3 topics, topic0 `[MAN].topics.LeafConsumed`) whose **emitter is `tx.to`** (the candidates), restricted to `topic2 == S6.Slot.Key` when `S6Status == s6_proven`; `foreign` = the `LeafConsumed` logs of other emitters; `anchorId := topic1` of the selected candidate [r3:S2-4 i] (it is not an input: the bundle-id recomputation and the `Batch` equalities of step 11 bind it to the proof file). The row table after this step decides every combination of `S6Status`, candidate count and emitter. The log's **emitter** is `account`; the account is identified by its emitter and its code (step 5), never by calldata. (c) S6 link (only when `S6Status == s6_proven`): `account == S6.Contract`, else `R s6_link_mismatch{field:account}`. (d) Path: `tx.to == account`, else `U settlement_path_unsupported{to,selector,reason}` - covering wrapper/relayer contracts, anchor-mediated `executeLegs` / `executeSingleLeg` (`CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:1182,1261`, both `onlyOperator`, which reach an account only through the anchor) and every other indirect call; the decoder fixes no calldata other than the one field of step 14. (e) After step 5 the **generation is the code**: the masked hash of `account` selects the `[MAN]` account build; `CertenAccountV7_3/r5` is the pinned generation and continues; a hash equal to a `pinned:false` row of `[MAN].generations` -> `U account_generation_unpinned{generation,code_hash,kind}` [r3.1:D2] (V7_2, V7, V6.x and the older generation measured in M12 land here once catalogued); a hash in no row at all -> `R code_not_published` (step 5); for `CertenAccountV7_3/r5` the calldata selector must be one of `[MAN].selectors.account.V7_3` else `U settlement_path_unsupported{to,selector,reason}`. [S6][MAN]
   *Step 3 row table [r3:S2-4 ii]* (`candidates` = the logs selected in (b); `foreign` = `LeafConsumed` logs of other emitters in the same receipt, e.g. a settled leg that itself settles another account):

   | S6Status | candidates | foreign | result |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | s6_proven | 1 | any | continue with (c)-(e) |
   | s6_proven | 0 | >= 1 | `U settlement_path_unsupported{to,selector,reason:"not_direct_call"}` (wrapper, relayer, anchor-mediated path) |
   | s6_proven | 0 | 0 | `U settlement_event_missing{count:0}` |
   | s6_proven | >= 2 | any | `U settlement_path_unsupported{to,selector,reason:"multiple_leaf_consumed"}` |
   | s6_silent or s6_not_proven | 1 | any | `account := emitter`; the part `s6_link` is `not_applicable{reason}` with `reason` = `s6_silent` or `s6_not_proven`, and for `s6_not_proven` additionally the Open entry `not_checked{part:s6_link, reason:s6_not_proven, state}` [r3.1:D12]; continue with (d)-(e): the generation is identified **by code** (step 5): the pinned `CertenAccountV7_3/r5` continues (S6 did not speak; S8's own provenance is intact), a `pinned:false` row (kind `catalogued` or `observed`) -> `U account_generation_unpinned{generation,code_hash,kind}` (the headline of the 71 of 86 recent Sepolia settlements, M12, M27), no row at all -> `R code_not_published` |
   | s6_silent or s6_not_proven | 0 | >= 1 | `U settlement_path_unsupported{to,selector,reason:"not_direct_call"}` |
   | s6_silent or s6_not_proven | 0 | 0 | `contract_identity_not_applicable{reason:"certen_infrastructure_call",to,role}` **only if** `tx.to` equals a `[MAN].deployments` row of the chain with `role` in {anchor, blsZkVerifier, groth16Verifier, accountFactory, outcomeRegistry} **and** no log of the receipt has topic0 in `[MAN].topics.accountEvents` (`GovernanceOperationExecuted`, `GovernanceBatchExecuted`, `LeafConsumed`); otherwise `U settlement_event_missing{count:0}` (an account call is not positively excluded) |
   | s6_silent or s6_not_proven | >= 2 | any | `U settlement_path_unsupported{to,selector,reason:"multiple_leaf_consumed"}` |

   `not_applicable` needs *positive* evidence that the transaction is not an account call; silence of S6 together with an absent event is `U`, never `not_applicable`. The r2 reason `"no_leaf_consumed"` is withdrawn. `S6Status` is derived by the `LegContext` builder [r3.1:D12]: `s6_proven` iff `ethproof.SettlementCallGeneration(tx.Data())` named a pinned generation (`replayguard.go:93-103`) and the `ReplayGuardCheck` state is `ReplayProven`; `s6_silent` iff S6 made **no claim** - the call generation is not pinned (`S6Reason: unsupported_generation`) or no S6 evidence exists for the leg (`absent`); `s6_not_proven` iff S6 **judged** the leg (the generation is pinned and S6 evidence exists) and its `ReplayGuardCheck` state is anything other than `ReplayProven` - the builder passes that S6 state verbatim (`S6State`, printed). A named S6 non-proof state is therefore never folded into silence: it is the Open entry `not_checked{part:s6_link, reason:s6_not_proven, state}`, which bars `verified` (not `verified_core`); for the `not_applicable` result of the last-but-one row the S6 state is printed beside it.
4. **Roots and S6 link.** `stateRoot_N` = item 3 of `Settlement.Header` (positional, `pkg/finality` helper; **not** `types.Header` decoding: `[S7]` s.0). The statement is judged against it; whether it is authenticated is step 24. S6 link (A2/D12; only when `S6Status == s6_proven`, else the part is `not_applicable{reason}` with `reason` = `s6_silent` or `s6_not_proven` [r3.1:D12]): `S6.SettlementBlock == Leg` (number and hash); if `S6.ProvenAt.hash == Leg.blockHash` (numbers equal too) the replay slot of S6 was proven under the very header S8 judges, so S6's read and S8's reads are under the same state root **by construction** (a header hash commits to its state root); else `S6.CodeHash` must equal the account code hash proven at `stateRoot_N` (the code is immutable; S6's later block only proves the slot, `replayguard.go:240-256`); any difference -> `R s6_link_mismatch{field in {account,block,proven_at,code_hash}}`. [r3:S2-4 iii] There is no `S6.StateRoot` and no accessor dispatch: `ReplayGuardCheck` (`pkg/ethproof/replayguard.go:280-296`, validator 0e10cb92) carries `SettlementBlock`, `ProvenAt` and `CodeHash`, which is all the link needs. [S6][S7]
5. **Account (settle).** Account proof of `account` at `stateRoot_N`: present, with code, `codeHash == keccak256(code[account])` (code carried) else `contract_identity_account_absent{role:account,address,root}` / `contract_identity_code_unproven_bytes{address}`; **masked** keccak (zero every `[start,start+length)` of `immutables[].references`, then keccak, the `[M]` `maskRule`; CBOR trailer included) equals `builds["CertenAccountV7_3/r5"].runtime.maskedKeccak` and length equals `runtime.bytes` else `contract_identity_code_not_published{role,address,code_hash,masked_keccak,want}` (this is the proxy / other-code refusal; a masked hash equal to a `pinned:false` row of `[MAN].generations` is instead the unproven state `account_generation_unpinned` of step 3e - an older legitimate generation is told apart from code in no row without ever widening a pin). [C][MAN]
6. **Account strings.** Read slot 0 (`adiURL`) and slot 11 (`governingBook`) with the string rule (short: data in high bytes and `2*len` in the low byte; long: `2*len+1`, data at `keccak256(slot)+i`); lengths <= cap; the container must prove exactly the implied data words. `adiURL` byte-equals `LegContext.adiURL` and `book` satisfies the factory rule `isGoverningBookOf(adiURL, book)` (`[C]:CertenAccountFactoryV11.sol:162`) else `contract_identity_account_not_canonical{reason:adi_url|governing_book}`. [C][CHAIN]
7. **Account immutables.** At every reference of a `constant` immutable (`_entryPoint`): the value of the manifest row `builds[].immutables[].rule.value` (`0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032`, the canonical ERC-4337 v0.7 EntryPoint), and the spec literal when the row carries none [r3.2:E-j] ([MAN] rule `constant`); of `owner`: `address(uint160(keccak256(bytes(adiURL))))`; of `governingBookHash`: `keccak256(bytes(book))`; all references of one immutable carry the identical 32-byte value (anything else is the same refusal): `contract_identity_immutable_mismatch{role,name,offset,got,want}`.
8. **Account provenance.** (a) CREATE2: `keccak256(0xff || F || salt || keccak256(creation || abi.encode(entryPoint, owner, adiURL, book)))[12:] == account` with `F` = the manifest `accountFactory` row [r3.1:D2] of the chain, `salt = uint256(keccak256(adiURL))` (canonical salt, `[C]:CertenAccountFactoryV11.sol:179`), `creation` = the embedded, manifest-hash-pinned bytes (`[M]` `accounts[].create2` is generated exactly so: `identity-manifest.mjs:799-802`); else `account_not_canonical{reason:create2}`. (b) Factory F at `stateRoot_N`: code masked-hash equals `CertenAccountFactoryV11/r5`, `entryPoint` immutables constant, `_deployedAccounts[account] == 1` (base 2), `_adiToAccount[keccak256(abi.encode(adiURL,book))] == account` (base 3, `[M]` storage rows) else `account_not_canonical{reason:registry|deployed_flag}` / code refusals as step 5. This closes F-S8-2. [MAN][C][CHAIN]
9. **Anchor pointer.** `account` slot 2 low 20 bytes = `A` (non-zero) must equal the **one** `[MAN]` `deployments` row with `role anchor` for the chain, else `contract_identity_pointer_mismatch{account,got,want}` (a decoy anchor with identical code, a pointer set by a first-caller `initializeAnchor`, or another chain's anchor). A pointer whose carried code masks to a `pinned:false` anchor row of `[MAN].generations` (V6, V6.1, V8, V8.1) is `U anchor_generation_unpinned{generation,code_hash,kind}`, not this refusal. The account's own pointer is the decisive one (`initializeAnchor` is first-caller, `CertenAccountV7_3.sol:322`); the anchor that **executed the attestation** is `A` by construction of step 17 (the `ProofExecuted` log emitter and the transaction target are `A`). The factory's `anchorContract` (slot 1) is reported as a consistency attribute, not required (the factory owner can change it, `CertenAccountFactoryV11.sol:198`). The code `contract_identity_address_not_published{role,address}` is used for the verifier, generated-verifier and factory addresses that are not rows of the chain. [CHAIN][MAN]
10. **Anchor identity (settle).** Account proof of `A`; code; masked keccak == `CertenAnchorV8_2/r5`; all 9 `DEPLOYMENT_CHAIN_ID` references equal `chainId` ([MAN] rule `chainId`). Refusals as steps 5/7.

(f2) *verifier rule on the INNER numbers* (blob words 14, 15) with the verifier's thresholds: `inner.signed x den_V >= inner.total x num_V` with the overflow guards of `BLSZKVerifierV2_1.sol:262-269` (an exact-ratio test, equivalent to `inner.signed >= ceil(inner.total x num_V / den_V)`; r1's label "ceil-rule" for the anchor's test was wrong, the anchor's is a floor); (f3) `inner == outer` on both numbers, else Open `alert inner_outer_differ{inner,outer}` (R-INNER, F-S8-8). The two tests differ: for total 10 and 2/3, floor gives `required = 6` (outer.signed 6 passes f1) while f2 needs `6 x 3 = 18 >= 10 x 2 = 20`, false, so inner.signed 6 fails f2 and 7 passes; for total 9, `required = 6` and `6 x 3 = 18 >= 9 x 2 = 18` holds - two boundary vectors in the plan; (g) **pkc tie (D10):** `pkc` is the blob's word 13 and word 12 equals `M` (step 17); words 14-15 are compared as in f3; (h) **governance rules [r3:S2-3]:** the rules PAUSED, GOVVERIFIER and MINGOV of the "Policy rules" table at pre and post: `_paused == 0` (else `R authorization_mismatch{field:paused,at}`); `governanceVerifier == 0` else `U governance_verifier_unpinned{address,at}` (the attestation was judged partly by an unidentified contract, `CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:2067-2078`); `minimumGovernanceLevel >= policy.minimumGovernanceLevel.min` else `R authorization_mismatch{field:minimum_governance_level,at}` (with level 0 an attestation passes with `keyBookRoot == 0`, `:2057,2094` [r3.1:D8]); and the decoded `governanceProof.authorityLevel >= minimumGovernanceLevel` (the contract's own test, `:2057` [r3.1:D8]; a failing tie is `R attest_mismatch{field:authority_level}`). The report prints `rules_judged` (the rule ids executed in steps 13, 19, 21) and `rules_not_judged` (the table's list, each with its reason) in every outcome. [CHAIN]
20. **Message binding.** `M == keccak256(abi.encode(bytes32("certen:bls:v2:pre"), uint256(chainId), anchorId, record.executionCommitment, record.operationID, currentValidatorSetRoot_pre, record.accSetRoot, record.accIncarnation))` (`CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:2141-2150`, with the step-11 record fields) else `R attest_mismatch{field:message_hash}`. With steps 17-19 this shows: the transaction the pinned anchor accepted carried a proof over a message that contains exactly the proven set root, and the contract accepts only when that equals its set root at that moment. [CHAIN]
21. **Registry, owner pin and registry link (A6).** (a) *Emit:* the report always carries `registry` = `{owner, root, threshold{num,den}, totalVotingPower, count, members[{address, power, registered, blsKey}], authorizedCommitments{count (slot 5), pkc, pkcAuthorized}, binding, verifier, governance{paused, governanceVerifier, minimumGovernanceLevel, minimumGovernanceLevelForValueOps}}` [r3:S2-3] as proven at B_v (post, and pre equal). (b) *Owner pin (D7):* the owners read in step 18 (`A` slot 27 and `V` slot 2) at pre and post equal a `policy.owner` row of the chain whose block range covers B_v, else `R authorization_mismatch{field:anchor_owner|verifier_owner,at}` (`at` in {attest_pre, attest_post} [r3.1:D2]): the owner is a pinned manifest fact, not a "stated trust input". (c) *Registry link:* if `Registry9` is present: member-by-member equality of (address, power, key bytes) with the on-chain `validators[]` at `stateRoot_post` (and pre), counts equal, `Registry9.thresholdNumerator/Denominator == anchor num/den`, `Registry9.certenSetRoot == currentValidatorSetRoot == root recomputed from Registry9 members` (`pkg/consensus/bls_registry.go:205`), the root inside the S9-signed message (L5 `Commitment.CertenSetRoot`) equal to `M`'s root component, else `R registry_mismatch{field}` [r3.1:D2] with `field` in {member_address, member_power, member_key, count, threshold, set_root, certen_set_root, message_root} [r3.5:H12] (`message_root` is the value of the internal detector only: it is never printed as the `field` of an `R registry_mismatch`; a pre-only change of `A14` is printed by F17 as `U state_changed_in_block{A14}`, see [r3.4:H1]): the first differing member by index gives `member_*`, the member counts `count`, `Registry9.thresholdNumerator/Denominator` `threshold`, the root recomputed from `Registry9` versus `currentValidatorSetRoot` `set_root`, `Registry9.certenSetRoot` `certen_set_root`, the root inside the S9-signed message `message_root`; key bytes compare as lowercase hex without `0x` (the stored registry and the on-chain `bytes` are identical, M17). If `Registry9` is absent [r3:S2-1]: let `row` be the `policy.setRootHistory` row of the chain whose range covers B_v and whose `root` equals `currentValidatorSetRoot` (A14, pre and post). No such row -> Open `not_checked{part:"registry_link",reason:"no_registry_in_file"}`. With a row, ALL of the following must hold at pre and at post, else the Open entry `not_checked{part:"registry_keys",reason,...}` with the reason named: (i) `row.keysDigest` present and equal to the digest recomputed from the proven keys, **`keysDigest = keccak256( STR("certen:validator-keys:v1") ‖ u32(n) ‖ for i in 0..n-1: B20(addr_i) ‖ LP(key_i) )`** with the addresses sorted ascending as `uint160` - the order of `_recomputeValidatorSetRoot` (`CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:1754-1790`) - and `key_i` the raw bytes of `validators[addr_i].blsPublicKey` (96 bytes live, M3), `STR`/`LP`/`u32` as `[S7]` s.0 (reasons `row_without_keys_digest`, `keys_digest_mismatch{want,got}`); (ii) `row.thresholdNumerator/Denominator` equal slots 15-16 (`threshold_mismatch`); (iii) `row.pkcCount` present, equal to slot 5 and to `len(row.pkcList)` (`row_without_pkc_count`, `pkc_count_mismatch{want,got}`), the list strictly ascending as `B32` (`pkc_list_malformed{index}`) and at most `max_pkc_list` 256† entries (`pkc_list_too_large{count,limit}`); (iv) every `c` in `row.pkcList` has `authorizedPubkeyCommitments[c] == 1` (rows A06; `pkc_list_absent` when the row has none, `pkc_set_mismatch{entry}` for the first entry that is 0). (iii) and (iv) together prove the authorized set **exactly**: slot 5 is the number of true entries (its only writer toggles it with each flag change, `:1861-1873`), so `pkcCount` distinct proven-true entries leave no room for another. All hold -> the part is verified `via:"manifest_history"` and the headline value is `registry_link: via manifest_history{keys:"digest",pkc:"exact_set"}`. An owner key swap with the root unchanged, an extra authorized commitment, or a replaced one never reads `verified`. [r3.1:D11] `pkc:"exact_set"` is defined as: the on-chain authorized set (the count in slot 5 and every entry of `row.pkcList`, proven at B_v) is **equal to the manifest `pkcList`**; it is NOT a statement that the set is quorum-only - that remains the residual R-PKC. **With a `Registry9` present, `registry_link` is a core part of the headline.** (d) *pkc cross-check:* `Registry9.SignerCommitment` (the aggregate-key commitment S9 already recomputes, `outcome_evidence.go:~44`; S8 does not reimplement MiMC, OD-S8-10) equals `pkc` else `R pkc_mismatch{s9,onchain}`; **an absent (zero) `Registry9.SignerCommitment` is the Open entry `not_checked{part:"pkc_signer_check",reason:"no_s9_commitment"}`** [r3:S2-2] (it bars `verified`, not `verified_core`; r2 had it only in the Named-states table); a report field `expected_subset_count` (the number of signer subsets with power meeting the threshold, enumerated when n <= 20) is printed beside the authorized count (slot 5) - necessary, not sufficient (R-PKC). [CHAIN] [r3.2:F17] `registry_mismatch` and `pkc_mismatch` obey the verdict precedence of the "Policy rules" table: `R` only when the compared on-chain words are equal at `attest_pre` and `attest_post` AND rule IB is verified; otherwise `U` with the state that table names (`state_changed_in_block`, `owner_active_in_block` or the IB `U` code). The root inside the S9-signed message and `Registry9.certenSetRoot` are one value in the frozen `Registry9` type: `message_root` is judged against `A14` at `attest_pre` (the root component of `M`) and `set_root` / `certen_set_root` against `attest_post`. [r3.4:H1] `message_root` is the detector of a pre-only change of `A14` on the registry link: it can fire only when `A14` at pre differs from the post word, and F17 prints that as `U state_changed_in_block{field:A14,pre,post,block}` on the part `registry_link`, never as `R registry_mismatch`; the vector `VS8-151.message_root` exercises exactly this branch.
22. **Intra-block window (rule IB; A3).** *Premise, from the pinned code [r3:S2-7 / M18]:* the table "AUTH slot set and writer premise" lists **every** function that writes an AUTH word - r2's list omitted `setGovernanceVerifier` `:1907`, `setMinimumGovernanceLevel` `:1913`, `setMinimumGovernanceLevelForValueOps` `:1919` (slots 29 and 30), `addOperator` `:1893` / `removeOperator` `:1897` and `invalidateIntent` `:1818` - and it is produced **mechanically** from the solc AST of the pinned build (manifest item 10), not by a grep. Every writer is `onlyOwner` (modifier `CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:653-656`; verifier `BLSZKVerifierV2_1.sol:140`) except the constructor, `createAnchor` / `createBatchAnchor` (guard `!anchors[bundleId].valid`, `:714` / `:856`, so they cannot touch the record, which is valid at B_v-pre), `executeComprehensiveProof` (the flips F1, F2) and `executeWithGovernance` (`onlyOperator`, byte 22 only, `:1416`); `executeLegs` and `executeSingleLeg` write no AUTH word. Indirect actors (`executeWithGovernance`, `executeSingleLeg` call arbitrary targets with `msg.sender == A`) can write an AUTH word only by calling an `onlyOwner` function of `A` or `V`, which needs `A.owner` or `V.owner` to equal `A`; both owners are the pinned EOA (A16 / V03, code-empty, M13). The premise holds only for builds whose `authWriters.status` is `pass` and whose allow-list is frozen (mechanical premise) [r3.1:D5]; the two `onlyOwner` modifiers are different pinned bodies (anchor `:653-656`, verifier `BLSZKVerifierV2_1.sol:140-143`). So a change inside B_v, kept or reverted, needs an execution with `msg.sender == owner`. *Checks:* (IB1) for each owner O in {`A.owner`, `V.owner`} (pinned in step 21b), the account proofs at `stateRoot_pre` and `stateRoot_post`: `codeHash` is the empty-code hash (or the account is absent) at both, and `nonce_pre == nonce_post`. A call with `msg.sender == O` for an account without code needs a transaction signed by O (nonce +1), an EIP-7702 delegation authorised by O (processing an authorization increments the authority's nonce), or - OP stack - a deposit transaction whose `from` is O, which increments the nonce too (`[OP]` "Nonce Handling"); no code at either boundary excludes a delegation active across the block boundary; equal nonces exclude all of them inside the block, including delegate-then-clear; O has a non-zero nonce (45 / 46 / 50 / 23, M13), and an address with a non-zero nonce cannot receive a contract. (IB2) *Census:* `blockTxs` rebuilt to `transactionsRoot(headerV)` (a different root, or `blockTxs[txIndex] != txLeaf`, is `R attest_mismatch{field:block_txs}` [r3:K]); every transaction type is in `policy.txScan[chain].coveredTypes` or `systemTypes` [r3:OQ-S8-10] (definitions and final lists: manifest item 2 and the table "Transaction types per chain"; a type is in a list only with a pinned source AND an on-chain observation [r3.1:D1]; measured types in the last 24 sampled blocks: Sepolia 0,1,2,3,4; Base 0,2 and 0x7E (2 per block); Arbitrum 0,2 and 0x6A (1 per block; the probe block of M24 also carried 0x68 and 0x69); Adiri 2, M15); any other type -> `U intra_block_window{reason: tx_type_unsupported{type,index}}`. (IB3) *States:* the anchor or verifier build row has no `authWriters` with `status` `pass`, or an allow-list that is not a subset of the frozen one -> `U intra_block_window{reason:build_without_writer_proof,build,condition}` [r3:S2-7]; owner has code -> `U intra_block_window{reason:owner_not_eoa{address}}`; nonces differ -> `U intra_block_window{reason:owner_active_in_block{address,pre,post}}` (this includes the benign case that the owner itself sent the attestation: unproven, not refused); too large (a capture that meets a block above the caps stores the attest part as `Stated{reason:block_too_large, detail:"bytes=<n>;limit=<m>"}`, because a file above a cap is refused at decode and never truncated) -> `U intra_block_window{reason:block_too_large{bytes,limit}}` [r3:K]. All hold -> the part is `verified` and its text is "no transaction of B_v executed as the owner". *Relation to the review's proposed scan (D2):* the review proposed carrying the transaction list and proving that no other transaction in B_v targets A/V/G/F or comes from the owner EOA. Rule IB is that scan made exact and cheaper: "comes from the owner" is decided by the owner's nonce and code, which also covers EIP-7702 delegations and OP deposits that a sender scan would miss; "targets A/V/G/F" needs no check because, by the writer analysis above, no non-owner transaction - direct or through any contract - can write an `AUTH` word other than the expected flips and byte 22. The transaction list is carried only so the type census (IB2) is proven against the header. [C][CHAIN]
22b. **Node accounting [r3.1:D11].** `NODES` must be **exactly** the set of nodes visited by the verifier's walks, so that one evidence has one container and seven validators that capture the same leg write byte-identical rows. After step 22 let V be the union of the nodes visited by every walk the run performed - every proof read of steps 5-22 (accounts, slots, strings, `bytes`, the transaction and receipt proofs of step 17, the hop and EIP-2935 reads of step 16), in the roots `settle`, `attest_pre`, `attest_post` and `hop:<i>`. The reads are fixed by the algorithm from the proven values and the context, so V does not depend on the implementation; a part's reads are all performed even when an earlier read of that part has already decided it `U` (the values are no longer used, the walks still count). A node of `NODES` that is not in V -> `R evidence_malformed{part:nodes, index:<index of the first such node>, reason:nodes_unreferenced}` (framework R, headline `refused`). The check is evaluated only when every read plan completed; when a read could not be derived because a prerequisite value is absent or invalid (a step 5-22 refusal), `nodes_unreferenced` is not raised on top of that refusal (the run trace, not the report, records the check as not evaluated) [r3.2:F2]. `Decode` (step 1) cannot apply this rule: it checks order and uniqueness only; the codec goldens G-S8-0/1/2 stay valid as codec goldens (Freeze item 1d).
23. **Report assembly and headline algebra (A1).** *Core parts:* `settlement_path` (3), `s6_link` (3c, 4; `not_applicable{s6_silent}` when S6 made no claim, `not_applicable{s6_not_proven}` plus its Open entry when S6 judged the leg and did not prove it [r3.1:D12]), `code_identity` (5, 10, 12, 18 code), `account_provenance` (6-8), `pointer` (9), `authority_level` (14) [r3:S2-5], `record` (11, with binding), `authorization_attest` (16-20), `intra_block_window` (22), and `registry_link` (21) **when a `Registry9` is present**. *Open entries:* `s6_link` `not_checked{s6_not_proven,state}` (step 3: a named S6 non-proof state) [r3.1:D12], `registry_link` `not_checked{no_registry_in_file}` (no `Registry9` and no manifest row), `registry_keys` `not_checked{reason}` (a manifest row that cannot prove keys or authorized set, step 21c) [r3:S2-1], `pkc_signer_check` `not_checked{no_s9_commitment}` (a `Registry9` without `SignerCommitment`, step 21d) [r3:S2-2], every `drift` / `alert` of `state_at_settlement` (13), `alert inner_outer_differ` (19f). Every outcome prints `rules_judged` and `rules_not_judged` [r3:S2-3]. A core part that is `not_applicable` (`s6_link` when S6 is silent) neither bars nor raises a headline: it is listed with its reason. *Headline* (first row that applies; the table still lists every part, S7 R2 style):

   | headline | when |
   |---|---|
   | `contract_identity_refused{first,parts}` (framework or judgement R) | a framework R (steps 0-2) or the framework R of step 22b (`nodes_unreferenced`) [r3.2:D15], or a judgement R while step 24 reports the state root authenticated [r3:n2] |
   | `contract_identity_pending{level_reached,next_level:"finalized",reason:"state_root_not_authenticated",findings:[{part,code,fields}]}` | a judgement R exists and step 24 reports the state root NOT authenticated [r3:n2]: the R states are facts about a candidate root; as in S7 a refusal is stated only against authenticated evidence, so the R codes ride in `findings` and the per-part table shows each such part as refused |
   | `contract_identity_unproven{parts}` | no R; at least one core part is U |
   | `contract_identity_pending{level_reached,next_level:"finalized",reason:"state_root_not_authenticated"}` | all core parts verified; step 24 not authenticated |
   | `contract_identity_verified_core{open:[{part,kind in {alert,drift,not_checked},code,...}]}` | all core parts verified; authenticated; at least one Open entry |
   | `contract_identity_verified{judged_at_level:"finalized",stateRoot,block,registry_link}` | all core parts verified; authenticated; **no Open entry** |
   | `contract_identity_not_applicable{reason:"certen_infrastructure_call",to,role}` | step 3 row table only [r3:S2-4] |

   `verified` therefore reports a `registry_link` value (`verified via S9 | via manifest_history{keys:"digest",pkc:"exact_set"}`) in its headline fields; `verified_core` is a distinct state, not a spelling of `verified`. The `residuals` (R-PKC, R-INNER, R-SETTLE-POINTER, R-WRITERS [r3.1:D5]) are printed in every report and are not Open entries. A `Stated` part or an Open entry can never raise a status (vector in the plan).
24. **Level binding.** `S7` result for `Leg`: `state_root_authenticated := (S7.finalized == verified && S7.finalized_block.hash == Leg.blockHash)`; `judged_at_level` = highest verified S7 level. Not authenticated -> the pending row of the table with all part results shown; authenticated -> proceed. A chain id not in the S7 table has no S8 statement [r3.1:D2]: `U unproven{part:all, reason:s7_chain_unsupported, chain}` (registry row `s7_chain_unsupported`, class U, headline `unproven`; the S7 code `finality_chain_unsupported`, `[S7]` R5, is carried in `s7_finalized_status`). A refused S7 `finalized` result is also "not authenticated" for S8; the report carries it as `s7_finalized_status` so a pending headline never hides it [r3:n2].

Interface (Go `pkg/contractidentity`; TS `packages/verify/src/proof-v2/identity/`, same names in camelCase; errors `{code, fields}` compared Go vs TS exactly as `[S7]` s.6):
```go
func LoadManifest(raw []byte, want [32]byte) (*Manifest, error)              // hash-checked; contract_identity_manifest_corrupt
func Decode(raw []byte, lim Limits) (*Container, error)                     // step 1
func Digest(d0 [32]byte, container []byte) [32]byte                          // Q2 item 4
type BatchFacts struct{ BatchRoot, OperationID, AccSetRoot, Incarnation [32]byte }       // all mandatory (step 1b)
type S6Status string // "s6_proven" | "s6_silent" | "s6_not_proven" [r3:S2-4] [r3.1:D12]
type S6Link struct{ Contract common.Address; LeafKey [32]byte; SettlementBlock, ProvenAt BlockRef; CodeHash [32]byte } // no StateRoot [r3:S2-4 iii]
type Registry9 struct{ Members []RegistryMember; Num, Den uint64; CertenSetRoot, SignerCommitment [32]byte }
type LegContext struct{ Settlement *ethproof.Settlement; Tx *types.Transaction; Receipt *ethproof.ReceiptLeaf; ADIURL string; S6Status S6Status; S6Reason string; S6State string; S6 *S6Link; Batch BatchFacts; Registry9 *Registry9 } // field table: Freeze inventory item 2 [r3.1:D12]
func Verify(ctx LegContext, c *Container, s7 finality.Report, m *Manifest) Report   // pure; steps 1b-24; Report.Headline is one of the six headline names of step 23 (refused, pending, unproven, verified_core, verified, not_applicable; `pending` has two rows, with and without `findings`)
type Verifier interface { Verify(ctx LegContext, c *Container, s7 finality.Report, m *Manifest) Report } // [r3:S2-6a] defined in WP-S8-1; WP-S8-3a's Append takes it by injection (nil is a construction error, no fallback); WP-S8-5 wires the real Verify
type Prover interface {
    CaptureAttest(ctx context.Context, chain uint64, anchorID [32]byte, blockV *BlockRef) (*Capture, *Stated)   // E1
    CaptureHop(ctx context.Context, chain uint64, from BlockRef) (*Capture, *Stated)                            // E1b tick
    CaptureSettle(ctx context.Context, s *ethproof.Settlement) (*Capture, *Stated)                              // E2
}  // may do I/O; every return is run through Verify at included level before it is stored
```

## Named states

Machine registry `testdata/contractidentity/states.json` (code -> required field names and class; an unregistered code is a conformance failure) [r3:K] - the complete, normative registry (one row per code and reason) is "Freeze inventory" item 3; the tables below keep the r2 reading order and `design/vectors/s8/regcheck.mjs` fails when a `contract_identity_*` token of this document is not a registry row, same canonical form as `[S7]` s.6 (`StateError`: sorted keys, integers as decimal strings, bytes as 0x hex; Go and TS compared). Every REPORTED state carries the report context `chain`, `block`, `block_hash`, `judged_at_level`, `manifest_sha256`, `manifest_source` beside (not inside) its own fields (Item 3) [r3.2:E-b]. Every way the evidence can be unavailable or insufficient has a code below; nothing is answered with a weaker value shaped like `verified`.

| class | codes |
|---|---|
| Framework R | `contract_identity_manifest_corrupt`, `contract_identity_manifest_unknown{chain}`, `contract_identity_manifest_shadow{table,key}` (r2), `contract_identity_evidence_unrecognised{kind,version}`, `contract_identity_evidence_malformed{part,index,reason,got_len,want_len}`, `contract_identity_evidence_too_large{part,count,limit}`, `contract_identity_block_mismatch{field,want,got}`, `contract_identity_context_incomplete{missing:[settlement,tx,receipt,adi_url,s6,batch.batchRoot,batch.batchOperationID,batch.accSetRoot,batch.incarnation,registry9,s7]}` (r2; list widened in r3, Freeze item 2) |
| Judgement R | `contract_identity_proof_invalid{root,address,slot}` (root in settle, attest_pre, attest_post, hop:i), `contract_identity_account_absent{role,address,root}`, `contract_identity_code_unproven_bytes{address}`, `contract_identity_code_not_published{role,address,code_hash,masked_keccak,want}`, `contract_identity_immutable_mismatch{role,name,offset,got,want}`, `contract_identity_address_not_published{role in {blsZkVerifier,groth16Verifier,accountFactory},address}`, `contract_identity_pointer_mismatch{account,got,want}`, `contract_identity_s6_link_mismatch{field in {account,block,proven_at,code_hash}}` (r2; `state_root` withdrawn in r3 [r3:S2-4 iii]), `contract_identity_record_not_executed{anchorId,valid,proofExecuted}`, `contract_identity_record_inconsistent{field in {bundle_id,merkle_root,operation_id,acc_set_root,incarnation}}`, `contract_identity_account_not_canonical{reason in {adi_url,governing_book,create2,registry,deployed_flag}}`, `contract_identity_authorization_mismatch{field,onchain,want,at in {settle,attest_pre,attest_post}}` (fields: set_root, threshold, verifier_threshold, binding, enabled, verifier, key, power, count, total_power, anchor_owner, verifier_owner, paused, minimum_governance_level [r3:S2-3]), `contract_identity_commitment_not_authorized{pkc,at}`, `contract_identity_attest_mismatch{field in {tx_to,selector,status,log,anchor_id,message_hash,flip,order,blob_layout,authority_level,block_txs}}`, `contract_identity_header_unlinked{link in {hops,spine},index,reason}`, `contract_identity_registry_mismatch{field}`, `contract_identity_pkc_mismatch{s9,onchain}` (r2), `contract_identity_authority_level_invalid{field,got}` (r3, step 14) |
| Unavailable / unproven (carried in `Stated` or derived) | `contract_identity_unproven{part,address,reason,...}` with reasons: `no_evidence_in_file`, `capture_not_attempted_in_window`, `state_unavailable`, `attest_block_state_unavailable`, `attest_block_out_of_reach{gap,window,hops_carried,last_hop}`, `attest_event_not_found`, `attest_indirect_call`, `attest_tx_type_unsupported{type}`, `anchor_generation_unpinned{generation,code_hash,kind}`, `account_generation_unpinned{generation,code_hash,kind}` (kind `catalogued` or `observed`, manifest item 12), `anchor_not_batch`, `governance_verifier_unpinned{address,at}` (r3), `record_created_in_block{block}` (r3), `authority_level_unproven{reason in {calldata_undecodable,too_many_legs,self_call_leg,level_log_missing,level_differs_from_logged,level_below_required_at_N}}` (r3; replaces `non_governing_book`), `settlement_not_executed`, `settlement_event_missing`, `settlement_path_unsupported{to,selector,reason}` (r2; replaces r1's `not_applicable` for wrapper / `executeLegs` / indirect paths), `code_not_carried`, and **`state_changed_in_block{field,pre,post,block}`** (r2: moved here from Judgement R), `intra_block_window` with `tx_type_unsupported{type,index}`, `owner_not_eoa{address}`, `owner_active_in_block{address,pre,post}`, `block_too_large{bytes,limit}`, `attest_absent`, `build_without_writer_proof` (r3, step 22) |
| Open (bar `verified`, not `verified_core`) | `contract_identity_not_checked{part,reason}` (registry_link: `no_registry_in_file`; registry_keys: `row_without_keys_digest`, `keys_digest_mismatch`, `threshold_mismatch`, `row_without_pkc_count`, `pkc_count_mismatch`, `pkc_list_absent`, `pkc_set_mismatch` [r3:S2-1]; pkc_signer_check: `no_s9_commitment` [r3:S2-2]; s6_link: `s6_not_proven{state}` [r3.1:D12]), `contract_identity_drift{field,attest,settle}`, `contract_identity_alert{field,at,onchain,want}` (settle-time policy violations: threshold, verifier_threshold, binding, enabled, owner; `inner_outer_differ{inner,outer}`) [r3:S2-5: the r2 code `unproven_attribute{authority_level,non_governing_book}` is withdrawn; `authority_level` is a core part now] |
| Pending | `contract_identity_pending{level_reached,next_level,reason:"state_root_not_authenticated"}` |
| Verified | `contract_identity_verified_core{open:[...]}` (distinct state), `contract_identity_verified{judged_at_level,stateRoot,block,registry_link}` |
| Not applicable | `contract_identity_not_applicable{reason:"certen_infrastructure_call",to,role}` (only on the step 3 row `s6_silent` / 0 candidates, with positive evidence that `tx.to` is CERTEN infrastructure) [r3:S2-4] |
| Headline wrappers (step 23) | `contract_identity_refused{first,parts}` (any R), `contract_identity_unproven{parts}` (no R, a core part U) - the per-part codes above ride inside `parts` |

Per-failure data to report (the runbook's `contract_identity_unproven{address, reason}`): the address, the part, the block and hash it was judged at, the root (settle/attest_pre/attest_post/hop:i), the provider failures (<= 64, text <= 1,024 B, redacted), and for generation/code cases the proven `code_hash` and `masked_keccak`. Builder-side failures to capture (insufficient proof window, lying provider, reorg between capture and block, a missed E1b tick) are stored as `Stated` parts or in a status table `proof_identity_status` outside any verifier input, as S7's status table (`[S7]` s.2.7).

## Test and vector plan

**Vector sources.** (1) Real containers, one per chain, captured live in RB13 from the live legs (the RB10 legs of M1 are the template; their proofs are no longer servable, R10 M8, so new legs). (2) A deterministic synthetic world builder (like `pkg/ethproof/replayworld` + `cmd/s6replayvectors`, `[V]:pkg/ethproof/testdata/s6replay1/SPEC.md` s.1): real code bytes from the manifest builds, real trie construction (geth trie) over a modelled state; fixed-seed mutation corpus (bounded, like S6's 781 cases at seed `0x56367265706c6179`). Pinned `MANIFEST` of file hashes; copied byte for byte into the SDK; TS never regenerates. New domain tag -> new goldens; nothing existing moves.

**Adversarial list (runbook Phase C, all required, each Go == TS on `code` + `fields`):**
1. proxy / other code at the address (EIP-1967-style bytes; code with right length and wrong body) -> `code_not_published`; code that does not hash to the proven codeHash -> `code_unproven_bytes`; truncated/padded code; CBOR trailer altered.
2. correct code, wrong immutable: anchor `DEPLOYMENT_CHAIN_ID` of another chain (one reference differing among nine), account `owner` not ADI-derived, `governingBookHash` not `keccak(book)`, wrong `_entryPoint`, verifier `groth16Verifier` pointing at a decoy generated verifier.
3. anchor pointer to another anchor (decoy with identical code and different registry; address not in the manifest).
4. verifier address swapped in anchor slot 30 (decoy with the same code but different threshold slots).
5. binding disabled at B_v (slot 6 = 0) - and the **N-only hole**: disabled at B_v, re-enabled before N; the naive runbook verifier (state at N only) accepts, the S8 verifier refuses. This is the design's fail-before (a faithful `NaiveSettlementOnly` implementation is kept in the test package as the negative control).
6. threshold changed: anchor (15/16), verifier (0/1), each at B_v.
7. commitment not authorized (`authorizedPubkeyCommitments[pkc] = 0`); pkc changed in calldata.
8. set root != registry root; registry with one extra / missing validator; power differs; key differs by one byte; `updateValidatorBLSKey` rotated between B_v and N (must verify: drift attribute).
9. storage proof for a different slot (slot-key swap, value-equal slot, mapping base off by one, array base+index vs the wrong manifest formula of F-S8-5).
**Beyond the runbook (mine):** account provenance (impostor account with same bytecode and `adiURL` at another address; CREATE2 mismatch; factory registry maps the ADI to another account; `_deployedAccounts` 0); string-slot forms (short vs long, wrong length word, missing data word); account absent (exclusion proof); empty storage root with a non-empty proof (S6 SPEC 4c); proof under the parent's root (stale), under N+1; settlement block/hash mismatch; `anchorId` / `leaf` mutated; `LeafConsumed` emitted by another address; `valid=0`, `proofExecuted=0` at N; bundle-id derivation broken; attestation: header V not matching the EIP-2935 value, EIP-2935 account code != pin (impostor history contract), wrong window rule (8191 applied on Arbitrum), gap beyond window with and without spine, spine break / reordered / too long, tx of another transaction, receipt without `ProofExecuted`, `tx.to` a wrapper (`attest_indirect_call`), type-3 tx, `message_hash` recompute mismatch (set-root component altered), pre != post for each AUTH word (one vector per word), `proofExecuted` already 1 at pre; container: unsorted / duplicate `NODES`, trailing byte, truncated, oversize, `encode(decode(x)) != x`, unknown kind, wrong magic; manifest: corrupt embedded copy (refuse to start), override with altered row, unknown chain, address not published; `Stated` parts of every reason (must never raise a status above `unproven`); Go vs TS disagreement on any of the above is stop-the-line (`00_STANDARD` s.3).
**Mutation gate** (`pkg/finality/mutgate_*_test.go` pattern): each step of the algorithm is disabled in turn and at least one vector must fail; **fail-before/pass-after**: the package is new, so the proof of "fails on base" is (a) vectors fail on the base commit because the package is absent, recorded in a throwaway detached worktree, and (b) the negative-control `NaiveSettlementOnly` accepts vector 5 while the real verifier refuses (the S7 B-GAP lesson, `[S7]` s.2.3: a first implementation that trusts the file's own claims). Real-block fixtures are built from the live legs; the first live container is verified under `golang:1.25` Docker for the timing line (`[S7]` s.11 item 3).
**What V-MANIFEST will add / must check** (already known from this pass): F-S8-5 (element formula), F-S8-7 (account mappings absent), manifest `policy` / `eip2935` / `selectors` / `topics` / `eip6780` sections (do not exist in v1), whether legacy generations (V6/V6.1/V8.1 anchors, V7/V7_2 accounts) should be listed as explicit `not_pinned` rows so the verifier can name them instead of guessing, per-deployment build variant (r5 vs r7) is already in rows, creation artifacts and their hashes, `OutcomeRegistry` (rows exist; not used by S8 v1, OD-S8-7), the Adiri single-account limit (RB12-B finding 4), and `slotChecks` coverage for `anchors[]` members and `isBatchAnchor`/`batchLeafCount`.

**Added in r2 (vectors required by the amendments; each Go == TS on `code` + `fields`):**
10. *Headline algebra (A1):* all core parts verified + one `alert` -> `verified_core{open:[alert]}`, never `verified`; + `drift` likewise; no `Registry9` and no manifest history -> `verified_core{open:[not_checked registry_link]}`; `Registry9` present and one key byte differs -> `refused registry_mismatch`; non-governing book -> judged by the stored page level (step 14; r2's `verified_core{open:[authority_level]}` is withdrawn in r3, VS8-082 / VS8-083); every `Stated` part and every Open entry tried against "raises status": none may.

## Freeze inventory (everything a Go implementer and a TS implementer need; machine-liftable tables) [r3:K]

Conventions: `[S7]` s.0 (`lp(x) = u32be(len(x)) ‖ x`, `LIST<T> = u32be(count) ‖ T…`, `STR = lp(ASCII)` without NUL, integers big-endian, `B20` / `B32` raw bytes, `u8` one byte). One table per item, one row per code; cells hold values, not prose, except the `note` column. The freeze package lifts these tables into `states.json`, the limits constants and the vector manifest; every code below is spelled with the prefix `contract_identity_` in `states.json` and in reports, and without it in the tables. Marker † = a round number nobody measured (raising it is a verifier release).

### Item 1 - CIE1 container, byte-exact

**No r3 amendment changes a container byte.** Every new read (`isBatchAnchor`, `batchLeafCount`, the `pkcList` entries, the step 14 level slots) is a derived slot proven inside `NODES`; `setRootHistory` rows, `authWriters` and the policy rules live in the manifest; `S6Link` and `LegContext` are never serialised. `design/vectors/s8/cie1.mjs` re-verifies G-S8-0 and G-S8-1 (M26): **unchanged**, both reproduce. G-S8-2 below is additive.

*1a Grammar (field order is the table order):*

| # | field | type / encoding | constraint | error when violated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | magic | 4 raw bytes `CIE1` | exact | `evidence_malformed{part:magic,reason:bad_magic}` |
| 2 | kind | `STR` `contract-identity/v1` | `STR` <= 64 B and exactly `contract-identity/v1` [r3.2:E-a] | a `STR` above 64 B: `evidence_too_large{part:kind,count,limit}`; a `STR` of at most 64 B that differs: `evidence_unrecognised{kind,version}`, `version` = the text after the last `/` as for S7 [r3.2:E-a] |
| 3 | chain | `u64` | equals the catalogue chain of the settlement | `block_mismatch{field:chain}` (step 2) |
| 4 | leg.number | `u64` | equals the number of `Settlement.Header` | `block_mismatch{field:number}` |
| 5 | leg.hash | `B32` | equals `keccak256(Settlement.Header)` | `block_mismatch{field:hash}` |
| 6 | codes | `LIST<Code>`, `Code = B20 address ‖ LP runtime` | count <= 16; addresses strictly ascending bytewise; runtime <= 262144 B | `evidence_malformed{part:codes,reason:codes_not_ascending or codes_duplicate}`; `evidence_too_large{part:codes}` |
| 7 | settle | `Part` | see 1b | see 1b |
| 8 | attest | `Part` | see 1b | see 1b |
| 9 | nodes | `LIST<LP>` | count <= 16384; each <= 131072 B (decode level; a state or storage trie node above 4096 B is `proof_invalid` at the walk); strictly ascending by `keccak256(node)`, unique; **and equal to the set of nodes the verifier's walks visit** [r3.1:D11] (not checkable at decode: step 22b) | `evidence_malformed{part:nodes,reason:nodes_not_ascending or nodes_duplicate}` (decode); `evidence_malformed{part:nodes,reason:nodes_unreferenced}` (step 22b); `evidence_too_large{part:nodes}` |
| 10 | end | - | no trailing byte; total size <= 4194304 B; `encode(decode(x)) == x` | `evidence_malformed{part:container,reason:trailing_bytes}`; `evidence_too_large{part:container}` |

**Parts and numbers of decode errors [r3.2:E-a].** The `part` of a truncation is the part of the read that failed; the reads of `chain`, `leg.number` and `leg.hash` are part `container`; the bound of the failure count and the bound of every `Stated` text are part `failures`; `index`, `got_len` and `want_len` of `evidence_malformed` are defined in `FORMAT.md` ("Decode error fields"); the reference script `cie1.mjs` follows this paragraph.

*1b Part:* `u8 tag` then the body. Tag 1 = captured: the `settle` body is **empty** (every read is derived and sits in `nodes`), the `attest` body is `Proof_attest`. Tag 2 = `Stated`. Any other tag -> `evidence_malformed{part,reason:unknown_part_tag}`.

| structure | fields in order | constraints |
|---|---|---|
| Stated | `STR state ‖ STR reason ‖ u64 judgedBlock ‖ B32 judgedHash ‖ LIST<ProviderFailure> failures ‖ STR detail` | `state` == `contract_identity_unproven` else `reason:bad_stated_state`; `reason` matches `[a-z0-9_]{1,64}` else `bad_stated_reason` (decode checks the syntax only; the closed list of the six builder reasons is a VERIFIER rule, step 1c: a carried reason outside it is `evidence_malformed{part,reason:unknown_stated_reason}`) [r3.2:E-f]; failures <= 64; every `STR` <= 1024 B, ASCII, no NUL else `string_not_ascii` / `evidence_too_large{part:failures}` |
| ProviderFailure | `STR host ‖ STR error` | as `STR` |
| Proof_attest | `u8 link ‖ LP headerV ‖ LP headerVParent ‖ [link 1: LIST<LP> hopHeaders] ‖ [link 2: LIST<LP> spine] ‖ u32 txIndex ‖ LP txLeaf ‖ LP receiptLeaf ‖ LIST<LP> blockTxs` | link in {0 same block, 1 hops, 2 spine} else `reason:unknown_link`; a header <= 4096 B†; `hopHeaders` count <= 16†; `spine` count <= 4096†; `txLeaf`, `receiptLeaf` <= 131072 B†; `blockTxs` count <= 4096† and total length <= 1048576 B†; links 0 and 2 carry no `hopHeaders`, links 0 and 1 carry no `spine` |

*Canonical orders:* `codes` ascending by address; `nodes` ascending by `keccak256` and equal to the set of nodes the walks visit (step 22b) [r3.1:D11]; `hopHeaders` ascending by block number (checked by the verifier, step 16); `spine` descending (step 16); `blockTxs` in block index order (typed wire encoding, EIP-2718).

*1c Limits (name = value, basis):*

| name | value | basis |
|---|---|---|
| max_container_bytes | 4194304 | `MaxReplayEvidenceBytes` precedent, Q1 |
| max_codes / max_code_bytes | 16 / 262144 | `pkg/finality` codec.go:43-50 |
| max_nodes / max_node_bytes | 16384 / 131072 | Q1 (†) |
| max_header_bytes | 4096 | † (r3) |
| max_attest_hops / max_attest_spine | 16 / 4096 | † Q1 |
| max_block_txs / max_block_txs_bytes | 4096 / 1048576 | † Q1, M15 |
| max_failures / max_text | 64 / 1024 | `MaxReplayProviderFailures`, `MaxReplayTextBytes` |
| max_validators / max_string | 64 / 1024 | Q1 |
| max_batch_legs | 64 | † step 14 |
| max_pkc_list | 256 | † step 21c |

*1d Goldens (all computed by `design/vectors/s8/cie1.mjs`, node `crypto` + its own keccak256 with a known-answer self-test):*

| id | content | bytes | sha256(container) | digest | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G-S8-0 | digest preimage for evidence `CIE1-test-vector`, D0 `1cea0a36...3445` | 103 (preimage) | `3ead3c1527420fcc681037f621f0d9362ce452f3496162d92fd47ab5e23d6923` (of the evidence) | `d7070fd59481084db1d6c97caf4cfb18865d4400a7a324a93799b39db7511edf` | unchanged since r2 |
| G-S8-1 | two `Stated` parts, no codes, no nodes (hex in Q2 item 4) | 379 | `d009d115af904ed12afed394efb75040986863137151d6d1ef05494d36793937` | `1102d40eacc348fce94b4995b4fe12f8b09e7770e4f7d7bdb972f4a9b58cd1d9` | unchanged since r2 |
| G-S8-2 | captured parts: 2 codes (`0x00..02` runtime `fe`, `0x01..01` runtime `6001600155`), `settle` tag 1, `attest` link 1 with hop headers `hop-1`, `hop-2`, txIndex 7, headerV `headerV-bytes`, headerVParent `headerVParent-bytes`, txLeaf `txLeaf`, receiptLeaf `receiptLeaf`, 2 block txs `tx0`, `tx1-typed`, 3 nodes `node-B-storage`, `node-A-state`, `node-C-tx` (all ASCII byte strings, in this order; the nodes are ordered by their keccak256, `node-B-storage` 50f036ed... < `node-A-state` d96906e9... < `node-C-tx` fb5a2dbe...; the byte strings are named in the paragraph below the hex) [r3.1:D11]; chain 11155111, leg (11845679, 32 x 0x22) | 303 | `8cf32b725e1c4ed69930f182012a7035a6d9ed2e68d4a5b931d7460e8bd1cab1` | `934aa97bcb306db1a15243b3b0552fdf1d20656be77ee3d236ccf121612684d1` | new in r3 (additive; specification only until WP-S8-1) |

G-S8-2 hex: ``

**Goldens and the node rule [r3.1:D11].** G-S8-0, G-S8-1 and G-S8-2 are **codec-level** goldens: they fix container bytes and the digest, and they are re-verified unchanged in r3.1 (`node design/vectors/s8/cie1.mjs` and `regcheck.mjs`, M26). G-S8-2's `NODES` and its other byte strings are arbitrary ASCII, not trie nodes, so it is not a verifiable container (no walk visits its nodes) and `Decode` must accept it: the unreferenced-node rule of step 22b is a verifier rule, not a codec rule. The G-S8-2 byte strings (ASCII; hex as they appear in the container): headerV `headerV-bytes` (`686561646572562d6279746573`), headerVParent `headerVParent-bytes` (`68656164657256506172656e742d6279746573`), hopHeaders `hop-1` (`686f702d31`) and `hop-2` (`686f702d32`), txLeaf `txLeaf` (`74784c656166`), receiptLeaf `receiptLeaf` (`726563656970744c656166`), blockTxs `tx0` (`747830`) and `tx1-typed` (`7478312d7479706564`), nodes `node-B-storage` (`6e6f64652d422d73746f72616765`), `node-A-state` (`6e6f64652d412d7374617465`), `node-C-tx` (`6e6f64652d432d7478`).

Worked example for the `keysDigest` of step 21c (live, illustrative, M28): Sepolia anchor `0x830cfB48...4E3c`, head 11978737, 7 validators with 96-byte keys, preimage 872 bytes, `keysDigest = 0x121bef0246b0b588d62106045f145c6bd4e2f5ffd2ad5dac4faa3efa75bb5173`, `pkcCount` 29 (`design/vectors/s8/pkcset.mjs`).

### Item 3 - named-state registry (one row per code and reason)

Classes: FR framework refusal; JR judgement refusal; U unproven (carried in `Stated` or derived, always `contract_identity_unproven` with `part` and `reason`); OPEN bars `verified`, not `verified_core`; PEND pending; VER verified forms; NA not applicable; WRAP headline wrapper. The common fields (chain, block, block_hash, judged_at_level, manifest_sha256, manifest_source) are the report CONTEXT, never merged into a state's own fields [r3.2:E-b]: a state's own fields are exactly the `fields` column (its `reason` included, see below); a field with a common name keeps its row meaning (`chain` of `manifest_unknown`; `block` of `state_changed_in_block` and `record_created_in_block`, which is the ATTEST block). **Canonical form [r3.2:E-b]:** in the vectors a state is `{"code","fields"}`, `fields` holding the row's own fields and its `reason` as one key (keys sorted, integers as decimal strings, bytes `0x` hex); in a Report it is `{"code","context","fields"}` with `context` the six common fields. **Reason [r3.2:E-c]:** a row whose reason cell is a plain reason (every `unproven` row except the families, `pending`, `not_applicable`) serialises that reason as the field `reason`; a `not_checked` row serialises `part` and `reason` from its cell; a FAMILY row (`authority_level_unproven`, `settlement_path_unsupported`: the cell names the family and the `fields` column lists `reason`) serialises ONE `reason`, the nested member of the Item 4 set of that name - the family name is a label of this table and is not serialised; a row whose `fields` column has no `part` carries no `part`, and every U row that lists `part` carries `part` and `reason`. **`refused.first` [r3.2:E-g]** is the FIRST REFUSAL STATE, the object `{code, fields}` of that state (its reason inside `fields`), not a string; `parts` are part names. Effect: `refused` (headline refused), `refused*` (headline refused when the state root is authenticated, else pending with findings, n2), `unproven` (headline unproven), `open` (verified_core), `pending`, `verified`, `na`. [r3.2:F14] The row `unproven | capture_not_attempted_in_window` carries no `address` field: a `Stated` part carries no address, so the field could not be filled from the evidence (the other Stated-carried unproven rows never had one). [r3.2:F17] `attest_absent` names the absence of ESTABLISHED attestation-block evidence: a `Stated` or absent `attest` part (step 15) AND a header link that step 16 refused or could not prove (steps 21 and 22 then decide `registry_link` and `intra_block_window` with this reason); it never means "verified but incomplete".

### Item 6 - CLI mapping (WP-S8-CLI; `verified_core` is never printed as, counted as or exit-coded as `verified`)

| headline | CLI text | exit code | counts as verified |
|---|---|---|---|
| verified | `contract identity: VERIFIED at <judged_at_level> (registry <via>)` | 0 | yes |
| not_applicable | `contract identity: not applicable (<reason>)` | 5 | no |
| verified_core | `contract identity: verified core, <N> open: <codes>` | 10 | no |
| pending | `contract identity: PENDING (state root not authenticated; <N> findings)` | 20 | no |
| unproven | `contract identity: UNPROVEN: <parts>` | 30 | no |
| refused | `contract identity: REFUSED: <first>` | 40 | no |
| (usage or internal error, including a recovered verifier panic: a Go error, never a Report) [r3.2:F3] | `proofverify: <error>` | 2 | no |

`verified_core` prints every Open entry as `<part>:<reason>` in the canonical order of Item 2b; a named S6 non-proof state prints as `s6_link:s6_not_proven(<state>)` and is counted, exit-coded (10) and printed as `verified_core`, never as `verified` [r3.1:D12].

## Work packages (token-sized; one branch and PR per phase; stack on the RB11 branches where named) - re-sized in r2 (A10), re-cut in r3 [r3:S2-6]

Sizes are token budgets per package including its own tests, fail-before proofs and check-in; the review found r1's WP-S8-2 (24 steps, MPT reads, ABI decode, CREATE2, EIP-2935, spine, pre/post, registry, level binding, mutation gate) at 130-170K about 2x low and WP-S8-3 (live capture under 25 s Arbitrum windows plus `pkg/execution` wiring) at the low edge and the riskiest `[REV]` section E. Every package below is <= ~170K; none may exceed it - a package that grows past it is split by its author before the work continues, with a check-in line.

**Dependency order, parallel groups and critical path (r3; S2-6)** (programme cap: 4 agents at once, `COMMON_RB12`). *Order:* 0a-i -> {0a-ii, 1}; 1 -> {2a, 2b-1, 2c, 3a, 7a}; 2b-1 -> 2b-2; {3a, 2b-1, 2b-2} -> 3b -> 3c; 2a -> 4a; {2b-2, 2c, 4a} -> 4b; {1, 2a, 2b-1, 2b-2, 2c, 3a} -> 5 -> 6; 7a -> 7b-1 -> 7b-2; CLI Go half after {2a, 2b-1, 2b-2, 2c}, TS half after 7b-2 (both consume the member shape of Q2 item 3; neither waits for 6) [r3.1:D9]; {4a, 4b, 7a, 7b-1, 7b-2} -> 8; {3a-3c, 5, 6, CLI} -> 10. *Parallel groups (each at most 4 at once):* G1 {0a-i}; G2 {0a-ii, 1}; G3 {2a, 2b-1, 2c, 3a}; G4 {2b-2, 4a, 7a}; G5 {3b, 4b, 5, 7b-1}; G6 {3c, 6, 7b-2, CLI-Go}; G7 {8, CLI-TS}; G8 {10}. *Critical path [r3.1:D9] (the metric is TOKENS - the sum of the midpoints of the size ranges along a dependency chain - not the package count):* 0a-i -> 1 -> 2b-1 -> 2b-2 -> 3b -> 3c -> 10 = 95 + 120 + 70 + 80 + 150 + 110 + 60 = 685K (seven packages; r2's path 0a -> 1 -> 3a -> 3b -> 3c -> 10 no longer holds because 3b now needs 2b-1 and 2b-2 to verify what it assembles); the next chains by tokens are 0a-i -> 1 -> 3a -> 3b -> 3c -> 10 = 665K, the TS chain 0a-i -> 1 -> 7a -> 7b-1 -> 7b-2 -> CLI-TS -> 10 = 635K and the Go chain 0a-i -> 1 -> 2b-1 -> 2b-2 -> 5 -> 6 -> 10 = 555K (the longest by package count, 7 against 6 after WP-S8-1, but not by tokens).

Consensus impact of all of the above: **none** - a new package, an additive migration, capture goroutines beside the observation (`pkg/execution` is not in the activation-freeze list; `pkg/consensus`, `pkg/proof`, `pkg/attestation`, `pkg/commitment`, `pkg/intentcert`, `pkg/proofv2shadow`, `pkg/ethproof` are not edited - `ethproof` is imported only; any needed export from `ethproof` is a separate dispatch that states its consensus-format impact); the evidence enters no attestation, govRoot or `ResultHash` input (S6 precedent, `[V]:pkg/chain/strategy/interface.go:411-419`). Prove "non-consensus deploy" by the same diff check as RB10 (no change to files that feed a hashed input). The one thing r2 adds that touches running processes: E1b ticks are new goroutines doing read-only `eth_getProof` at head.

## Decisions OD-S8-1..13 (all resolved in r2; the orchestrator may object in one line, see the final table)

- **OD-S8-1 Attestation station V in kind v1.** **DECIDED: mandatory** (forced by the source: the quorum is judged at TX2, F-S8-1; the review confirmed `[REV]` F-S8-1). An N-only kind is the negative control `NaiveSettlementOnly`, not a product.
- **OD-S8-2 Headline policy.** **DECIDED, changed from r1** (D1): the headline is the six-row algebra of step 23. Core parts include `intra_block_window`, mandatory record binding and - when a `Registry9` is present - `registry_link`; `state_at_settlement` and `authority_level` are Open entries that bar `verified` but not `verified_core`; `verified` only when nothing is open. The r1 reasoning (a registry rotation after the attestation must not void old settlements) is kept by making settle-time facts `drift`, not refusals.
- **OD-S8-3 Account provenance.** **DECIDED: both** CREATE2 recomputation (verifier embeds hash-pinned creation code, ~15.7 KB per verifier binary, nothing per proof) and the factory registry/code (~28 KB per proof). Live arithmetic 13/13 (`[REV]` F-S8-2).
- **OD-S8-4 Manifest v1.1** before verifier work. **DECIDED: yes, WP-S8-0a-i first (0a-ii for the generations; r3 adds items 9-12)**, with the eight items of the section list (D13).
- **OD-S8-5 Capture ownership.** **DECIDED: every validator captures on E1, E1b and E2, durable, insert-only.** Measured topology (M11): the seven validators and the proof service share one Postgres `certen_proofs`, so seven identical writes of the same `(chain, anchor_id, block_hash, item)` are a byte-equal no-op and a difference is `ErrCaptureConflict` - items are stored as canonical (sorted, de-duplicated) node sets so equal captures are byte-equal.
- **OD-S8-6 Serving form.** **DECIDED:** new portable member `contractIdentity` + two insert-only tables (not an S7 addendum kind, not a JSON blob inside L6).
- **OD-S8-7 OutcomeRegistry / outcome path.** **DECIDED: out of S8 v1.** The registry's record block needs its own S7 binding; the claim text names account and anchor. This is an owner-visible scope note (Owner-gated list), not silent.
- **OD-S8-8 Status tokens.** **DECIDED:** `pending` while S7 is below `finalized`; no "verified at included" token. Step 23 adds `verified_core` as a distinct state (it is not a lower-level `verified`).
- **OD-S8-9 Policy constants** (threshold 2/3, binding on, enabled on, verifier 2/3, owner history, tx types) as manifest `policy` rows, not code constants. **DECIDED.**
- **OD-S8-10 pkc vs signers' aggregate key.** **DECIDED:** S8 reports `pkc`, requires it authorized, and requires equality with S9's recomputed `SignerCommitment` when a `Registry9` is present (step 21d); no MiMC reimplementation in S8; the pkc-subset residual R-PKC is stated.
- **OD-S8-11 Later-static station for legs whose capture was missed.** **DECIDED: reserve `contract-identity/v2` grammar space, build nothing now.** Recorded reading (D14, for the orchestrator's run log): this is acceptable only because the definition of done is *fresh* live proofs (`00_STANDARD` s.8.1) and stored legacy proofs keep their verdicts (s.8.3); a missed capture is a named state, never a silent gap; the station needs the OD4 archive provider and S7 spine states. If the owner reads the DoD as requiring repair of missed captures, this decision reverses and the station becomes a package.
- **OD-S8-12 Adiri source.** **DECIDED: CERTEN's own node for the Adiri pre-state** (needs OQ-R11-3, owner-gated); until then Adiri S8 is `unproven{attest_block_state_unavailable}` by design. Adiri `verified` in the DoD is blocked on it; the implementation is not.
- **OD-S8-13 EIP-2935 reach.** **DECIDED, changed from r1** (D6): the 2935 link **with a hop chain** (E1b, `link 1`, reach 16 x floor(W/2) + W [r3.4:H8]) plus the spine for chains without the history contract; `attest_block_out_of_reach` remains only for a broken tick chain and for legs that pre-date E1b - an owner-acknowledged named limit (Owner-gated list). Base post-Denim W = 27.3 min (M14) against 30 min per settler and ~50 min takeover (`batch_settlement_window.go:68`) makes the hop chain necessary, not optional, for `verified` on Base takeover legs.

Added in r2 (each is a design choice the review's fixes force; object by ID):
- **OD-S8-14 Intra-block rule.** **DECIDED: rule IB** (owner EOA code-empty and equal nonce at B_v-pre/post + transaction-type census of B_v) rather than per-transaction ECDSA sender recovery. Reason: the nonce argument is exact for ECDSA, EIP-7702 and OP deposits (`[OP]`), needs no secp256k1 in the verifier, and is two account proofs; the census is what keeps it sound against non-nonce transaction types.
- **OD-S8-15 Owner pin.** **DECIDED: `policy.owner` history rows** (rotation = manifest append + verifier release; a rotation before the append makes legs `authorization_mismatch{anchor_owner}`, which is the point).
- **OD-S8-16 Migration number.** **DECIDED:** "next free migration number at merge" - never a fixed number (00029 is also claimed by RB12-DBFIX).

Added in r3 (each is a design choice the re-review's fixes force; object by ID):
- **OD-S8-17 manifest_history exactness [r3:S2-1].** **DECIDED: `verified via manifest_history` requires `keysDigest`, `pkcCount` AND `pkcList` (exact set).** Stronger than the review's minimum (`keysDigest` + count): a count alone cannot see a *replaced* authorized commitment (count unchanged), and a replaced commitment is exactly what would let a non-registry signer set attest, because the circuit places no constraint on which key signed (`CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:2223-2227`). Cost: at most 2 x `|pkcList|` extra slot proofs (29 live, about 40 KB at the measured proof sizes); cap `max_pkc_list` 256 (dagger), a longer list -> `not_checked{registry_keys,pkc_list_too_large}`.
- **OD-S8-18 governanceVerifier [r3:S2-3].** **DECIDED: a non-zero `governanceVerifier` is never pinnable in v1** (`U governance_verifier_unpinned`); the review's "or a pinned manifest row" is not adopted because no GovernanceVerifier build exists to pin (live value zero on all four anchors, M22) and S8 has no semantics for one; a judged build is a `contract-identity/v2` item.
- **OD-S8-19 `observed` generation rows [r3:S2-6c].** **DECIDED: `U account_generation_unpinned{kind:"observed"}`** - never `verified`, never `R`. A family announced by a CERTEN factory (`AccountDeployed`) has established CERTEN provenance but unpublished code; a refusal would claim a mismatch against a published build that nobody can produce, while `R code_not_published` stays for code in no row at all. The `kind` field makes the two readable apart.
- **OD-S8-20 Verifier injection [r3:S2-6a].** **DECIDED:** WP-S8-1 defines the `Verifier` interface, WP-S8-3a's `Append` takes it by injection, WP-S8-5 wires the real one; 3b depends on 2b-1 and 2b-2.
- **OD-S8-21 txScan semantics [r3:OQ-S8-10].** **DECIDED:** `systemTypes` = types that never run contract code, no sender rule; `coveredTypes` = run code as `from` and increment its nonce; Base 0x7e moves from system to covered (M19). [r3.1:D7] The classification rule is the ONE rule of the table "Transaction types per chain" - a pinned source AND an on-chain observation, for every type of every chain.
- **OD-S8-22 R under an unauthenticated root [r3:n2].** **DECIDED:** `pending` with `findings`, mirroring S7 (a refusal is stated only against authenticated evidence); framework R is unaffected.
- **OD-S8-23 authority level [r3:S2-5].** **DECIDED:** `authority_level` is a core part; `self_call_leg` and `level_below_required_at_N` are `U`, never `R`.
- **OD-S8-24 First-live acceptance thresholds [r3:J].** **DECIDED** (numbers are decisions, not measurements; object by ID): AT-4, AT-6, AT-9, AT-11 of "Open questions".
- **OD-S8-25 Types without an observation [r3:OQ-S8-10] [r3.1:D1] [r3.1:D7].** **DECIDED:** a type is a manifest `covered` / `system` row only with a pinned source citation AND an on-chain observation; a type with a source but no observation stays `tx_type_unsupported` on that chain (Arbitrum 0x1, 0x78; Base Sepolia 0x1, 0x3; Adiri 0x1, 0x3, 0x4) and moves into the manifest by a manifest release that appends the observation (block, tx hash, nonces, command) and the source line, e.g. from `design/vectors/s8/arbtypes.mjs` or `typeobs.mjs` on a live transaction of that type. Nothing is assumed from a source alone.
- **OD-S8-26 Logged versus recomputed level [r3.1:D6].** **DECIDED: `U authority_level_unproven{level_differs_from_logged}`, not `R`.** The dispatch named an `R attest_mismatch`-class refusal or "the nearest existing row"; the nearest existing row by class is `authority_level_unproven` (U), because the recomputation reads the END state of block N and a later transaction of N can legitimately change the words (R-SETTLE-POINTER), so a difference does not PROVE a wrong level; `R` would refuse honest settlements.
- **OD-S8-27 S6 non-proof state [r3.1:D12].** **DECIDED:** `s6_not_proven{state}` is an Open entry (bars `verified`, not `verified_core`); `s6_silent` means only "S6 made no claim".
- **OD-S8-28 Writer gate [r3.1:D5].** **DECIDED:** the gate is member-level; the allow-list is frozen in the verifier (a manifest allow-list wider than it is `build_without_writer_proof{allowlist_not_frozen}`); what the build cannot prove about the extractor is the printed residual R-WRITERS.
- **OD-S8-29 Canonical node set [r3.1:D11].** **DECIDED:** `NODES` equals exactly the union of the visited nodes (`evidence_malformed{nodes,nodes_unreferenced}`, step 22b); the codec goldens are unaffected.
- **OD-S8-30 Arbitrum `0x4` [r3.1:D1].** **DECIDED: covered** (departure from the dispatch list, which had it unsupported): the rule "pinned source AND on-chain observation" is met by blocks 316000280 and 316000385 (M29).

## Measurements (all 2026-10-23 UTC unless noted; commands are reproducible with `cast`/`node`)

**M1 - attestation-to-settlement gap on the four live RB10 legs.** Settlement receipts via `cast receipt <tx> --rpc-url <chain>`; anchorId = `LeafConsumed` topic1; `cast logs --address <anchor> --from-block <N-span> --to-block <N> 0xaafab89926d77fbd622e61cfa62ca5de53bbde4f6686f2c46842b4e3a41f767d <anchorId>` (topic0 = `cast keccak "ProofExecuted(bytes32,bytes32,bool,bool,bool,uint256)"`). Output: Sepolia anchorId `0x99c1b734...8820`: ProofExecuted block 11950123 (tx `0xa246887dab...`), settlement 11950125 -> 2 blocks; Base Sepolia `0x12702b81...9e79`: 48333019 (tx `0xd1d08363cb...`) -> 48333021, 2; Arbitrum Sepolia `0x990d27b1...6750`: 320818467 (tx `0xec698cff0a...`) -> 320818474, 7; Adiri `0x26cb08b4...1c79`: 513642 (tx `0x16875a24d2...`) -> 513643, 1. Conclusion: in the live pipeline TX2 and TX3 are separate transactions in separate blocks 1-7 blocks apart (F-S8-1 holds on all four chains); the gap is not fixed: it is bounded by the leaf `notAfter` (`CertenAccountV7_3.sol:587`) and `proof.expiresAt` (`:536`) - for a takeover settler up to about 50 min after the attestation (`SettlementWindow = 30 min`, `batch_settlement_window.go:68`).
**M2 - the attestation transaction.** (selector re-derived from the source: `cast sig` of `executeComprehensiveProof(bytes32,(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32[],bytes32,(string,bytes32,bytes32[],address,uint8,uint256,uint256,uint256,bool),(bytes,address[],uint256[],uint256,uint256,bool,bytes32),(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32,bytes32,string,uint256,bytes32,string,address),uint256,bytes))`, the struct definitions of `CertenAnchorV8_2.sol:429-474`, = `0x4ca9d0c8`, equal to the live value.) Base Sepolia tx `0xd1d08363cb5e3658b9d10b42ff4c6a3796f88bca9cbf79af71634195f35a6d79`: type 2, `to` = anchor `0x830cfb48...`, `from` = `0xee2efa29...45fe` (a registered validator), input 2,660 B, selector **`0x4ca9d0c8`**, tx index 40 in block 48333019. **M28 - exact-set mechanism and `keysDigest`, live (S2-1).** `node design/vectors/s8/pkcset.mjs https://gateway.tenderly.co/public/sepolia https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com 0x830cfB484b6e5606687e00f64C40aeb9c7c84E3c 11832000` (48 RPC calls; events from the Tenderly gateway, state from publicnode at head 11978737): the `PubkeyCommitmentAuthorized(bytes32,bool)` events folded give **29** authorized commitments and no revoked one; slot 5 reads 29; `authorizedPubkeyCommitments[c]` (slot `keccak256(abi.encode(c, 4))`) reads 1 for every one of the 29; `validatorList` length 7, every `validators(addr).blsPublicKey` is 96 bytes; `keysDigest = keccak256( STR("certen:validator-keys:v1") ‖ u32(7) ‖ 7 x (B20 address ‖ LP key) )` over the addresses ascending, preimage 872 bytes (= 28 + 4 + 7 x 120), = `0x121bef0246b0b588d62106045f145c6bd4e2f5ffd2ad5dac4faa3efa75bb5173`, equal to `cast keccak` of the same preimage (and to the script's own keccak256, whose known-answer self-test is M26). Conclusion: the count-plus-list proof of step 21c holds on the live anchor, and the digest definition is implementable in Go and TS without an ABI encoder. The value is a worked example of the live state at that block, not a pin.
